project_description: The requirements definition of OpenV itself: multi-agent development suite, multi-tenant SaaS, predictable BYO-AI execution.

artifacts.title: Personal spaces
artifacts.body: Every user shall automatically receive a personal workspace on registration.

artifacts.title: Company workspaces
artifacts.body: Companies shall have workspaces with admin and member roles, and named teams of users.

artifacts.title: Per-project access grants
artifacts.body: Project access shall be grantable per user and/or per team, with role levels (owner, editor, viewer); a member's effective role is the highest of their direct and team grants.

artifacts.title: Authentication
artifacts.body: The system shall support email and password session authentication, Google sign-in, and sign-in through a generic OpenID Connect provider an operator configures. The system shall bind an account to the first identity provider it signs in with and shall refuse a later sign-in for the same email through a different provider. The system shall hash passwords with bcrypt and shall refuse a password shorter than eight characters.

artifacts.title: Workspace deletion
artifacts.body: A workspace admin shall be able to delete a company workspace. Deletion hides and locks the workspace immediately for all members; its projects and data are retained and restorable by a workspace admin for 30 days, after which the workspace and all contained data are permanently deleted by a scheduled purge. Personal workspaces cannot be deleted.

artifacts.title: Workspace AI budget and usage
artifacts.body: The system shall let a workspace admin set a monthly AI spend budget for the workspace and shall show each workspace its month-to-date usage. The system shall notify the workspace admins once when usage reaches 80 percent of the budget and once more when it reaches 100 percent, at most once per threshold per month. When an operator enables budget enforcement, the system shall refuse to launch a new run in a workspace that has exhausted its budget; otherwise the system shall warn only.

artifacts.title: Plan limits
artifacts.body: Each workspace shall carry a plan whose defaults bound the resources a runner may use: hosted runner memory and CPU, transient lease lifetime and idle window, and the first-refusal grace window. A workspace shall be able to override an individual limit, and the system shall fall back to the plan default for any override that is missing or not a number, so that a corrupt setting never yields an unbounded limit.

artifacts.title: Observability
artifacts.body: The system shall expose an unauthenticated liveness endpoint, a Prometheus metrics endpoint that an operator can gate with a bearer token, and a structured request log that names the resolved workspace, user and actor kind on every line. Metrics shall be labelled by route template, method and status only, never by project, user or agent, so that cardinality stays bounded. The system shall record HTTP request counts and latency, run lifecycle counts and gauges, and live stream connection counts.

artifacts.title: Backup and restore
artifacts.body: The self-hosted stack shall produce one timestamped backup bundle holding a database dump, the data volume and the uploads volume, on demand and on a configurable schedule, shall write a bundle under a temporary name and rename it only on success, and shall prune bundles older than a configurable retention. The stack shall restore any such bundle. On a managed platform the operator documentation shall state which of those three stores the platform's own backups cover and which the operator must back up separately.

artifacts.title: Forward-only schema migration
artifacts.body: The system shall advance the database through a numbered migration ledger at startup, applying each migration exactly once inside its own transaction together with its ledger row, under a database lock so that concurrent instances never apply a migration twice. A failed migration shall leave neither the schema change nor its ledger row behind. The system shall never edit an applied migration.

artifacts.title: Define products without a team
artifacts.body: As a solo founder I need to define one or more products and manage their complete requirement sets on my own, so that I can run a real product process without hiring.

artifacts.title: Guided requirements definition
artifacts.body: I need step-by-step, conversational guidance that turns rough product ideas into structured requirements, because I am not a requirements engineer.

artifacts.title: AI does real work under my control
artifacts.body: I need AI agents to perform meaningful requirements and development work, while every change they make passes through my explicit approval.

artifacts.title: Bring my own AI
artifacts.body: I need to use the Claude, GPT or Gemini subscription I already pay for, and my company needs its own metered API-token AI - not platform-marked-up inference.

artifacts.title: One view of human and AI work
artifacts.body: I need a single board that shows what both my human colleagues and my AI agents are working on, so nothing falls between the two.

artifacts.title: Company workspaces and access control
artifacts.body: My company needs private workspaces with admins, teams and per-project access so different groups can work without seeing each other's data.

artifacts.title: Audit-ready traceability
artifacts.body: I need end-to-end traceability from stakeholder needs through requirements to verification evidence, so the product can face audits and regulated customers.

artifacts.title: Capture stakeholder input effortlessly
artifacts.body: I need to gather requirements from internal and external people who will never open a requirements tool - a link they can click and just talk.

artifacts.title: Predictable agent execution
artifacts.body: I need agent work to start reliably regardless of which colleague is online, while runs I launch still prefer my own machine and subscription first.

artifacts.title: Nothing runs without my consent
artifacts.body: I need certainty that OpenV runs nothing in the background on my machine: a runner executes only while I have deliberately opened it, and stops when I close it.

artifacts.title: Demo material I did not have to invent
artifacts.body: As someone trying, demoing or testing OpenV I need a supply of believable throwaway products to drive the wizard with, so that I never have to spend a real product idea or type a fake one to see the tool work. Because that material now comes from other people, I also need whatever reaches my screen and my agent's context to be inert, attributable and removable.

artifacts.title: Run it myself without an operations team
artifacts.body: As a solo founder or company admin I need to run OpenV on my own host or on a managed platform, keep its data safe, see that it is healthy, and know that the parts exposed to the internet are hardened, because I have no operations or security team to do that for me.

artifacts.title: Act on my product from my phone
artifacts.body: As a founder, admin or contributor away from my desk I need to approve or reject what my agents and colleagues propose, read the requirement someone linked, answer a comment or ask the assistant, move a board card, and start a cloud runner and sign an agent in, all from my phone or tablet, because the work does not wait for me to be at a desktop and nothing should need installing.

artifacts.title: SEC-1 Prompt injection into auto-approving vendor CLIs
artifacts.body: Severity: High. Affects: self-hosted and Railway. Runners start Gemini with --approval-mode auto_edit (internal/runner/geminicli.go:112) and Codex with --sandbox workspace-write and no tool allowlist (codexcli.go:140); Claude Code receives an allowlist only when the agent defines one (claudecode.go:158). Untrusted text reaches those prompts: the public interview transcript is concatenated into the interviewer prompt (internal/api/suite_handlers.go:1528) and that agent holds the OpenV tools; repository-access agents run inside a real checkout; the V&V Assistant fetches web pages. An external participant, a repository file or a web page can therefore carry instructions the CLI acts on with auto-approved edits or commands, and proposal gating protects OpenV data only, not the runner host or its credentials. Recommendation: REQ-91.

artifacts.title: SEC-2 Hosted runner containers lack isolation hardening
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium. Affects: self-hosted only (hosted runners are off on Railway). internal/hosting/docker.go:84-115 sets memory and CPU caps but no capability drop, no no-new-privileges, no read-only root, no pids limit and no dedicated network; provider API keys enter as container environment; the API itself holds the host's Docker socket when the feature is enabled (docker-compose.yml). Combined with SEC-1 a compromised agent reaches the host and long-lived keys. Recommendation: REQ-96.

artifacts.title: SEC-3 Tenant-chosen api_key_env reads any runner host variable
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium. Affects: both. Provider settings validate provider and auth mode but not the api_key_env name (internal/domain/providers/providers.go:66,160-181); the worker reads os.Getenv on that name and injects the value into the agent's environment (internal/runner/worker.go:368). A workspace admin can name WORKER_API_KEY, RUNNER_POOL_KEY, DATABASE_URL or any other host variable, and an agent (SEC-1) can then read it. Recommendation: REQ-92.

artifacts.title: SEC-4 Weak development defaults in the base compose stack
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium. Affects: self-hosted only. docker-compose.yml runs Postgres with password "postgres" and publishes port 5432 on the host, and defaults WORKER_API_KEY to "dev-worker-key"; the backup sidecar falls back to the same password. The production overlay correctly makes these required and unpublishes the port, so the exposure is a deployment that runs the base file on a reachable host. Recommendation: REQ-97.

artifacts.title: SEC-5 No throttling on sign-in, registration or run launch
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium. Affects: both; confirmed live on production 2026-09-06 (eight failed sign-ins in under two seconds all answered 401 with no back-off). Rate limiting exists only on the public interview endpoints (internal/api/handlers.go:233-235). bcrypt slows guessing but nothing locks or throttles an account or an address, and the limiter is in-memory and single-instance. Recommendation: REQ-90.

artifacts.title: SEC-6 SVG attachments served inline with uploader-supplied type; no body size limit
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium. Affects: both. image/svg+xml is an accepted image type (internal/api/handlers.go:2335), the client-supplied MIME type is stored, and downloads are served with Content-Disposition inline (handlers.go:2275), so an SVG carrying script executes on the API origin for a viewer who opens the download URL directly. Uploads are read with io.ReadAll and no MaxBytesReader, and a 2 MB JSON body to the sign-in endpoint was accepted on production. Mitigated by viewer authentication on download and the SPA rendering images through img tags only. Recommendation: REQ-93.

artifacts.title: SEC-7 Known-vulnerable docker/docker module compiled into the API
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium self-hosted, Low on Railway. govulncheck reports GO-2026-4887 and GO-2026-4883 in github.com/docker/docker v28.5.2 (no fixed version yet), reachable through internal/hosting/docker.go, plus six advisories in required-but-not-called modules. Railway runs with HOSTED_RUNNERS=off so the code path is dormant there. Recommendation: bump when a fix ships; REQ-98.

artifacts.title: SEC-8 Frontend production dependency advisory (fast-uri)
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: both. npm audit --omit=dev reports one high advisory in fast-uri 3.0.0-3.1.5, a transitive build-time dependency with little runtime exposure in the static bundle. Recommendation: bump the override pin; REQ-98.

artifacts.title: SEC-9 Live invite tokens written to the request log
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: both. The request log records the URL path (internal/api/requestlog.go:62) and the public interview routes carry the raw invite token in the path, so anyone with log or proxy access holds a live token until it expires. Tokens themselves are strong (32 random bytes, stored as SHA-256). Recommendation: REQ-97.

artifacts.title: SEC-10 API image runs as root
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: both. Dockerfile.api has no USER directive, so the API process runs as root inside its container; the frontend (USER nginx) and worker (USER worker) images already drop privileges. Recommendation: REQ-97.

artifacts.title: SEC-11 No browser security headers reach production; CSP permissive by design
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium on Railway, Low self-hosted. frontend/nginx.conf declares X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and a CSP at server level, but every location block adds its own add_header (caching), and nginx drops inherited add_header directives in any location that sets one. Confirmed live on 2026-09-06: the production frontend and its static assets return none of those headers, and the API returns no HSTS, nosniff or frame header on any response. The declared CSP is also permissive (unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval, any http/https origin). Recommendation: REQ-94.

artifacts.title: SEC-12 Backups unencrypted and on-host by default
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: self-hosted only. scripts/backup.sh writes a plain tar.gz holding a full pg_dump (accounts, bcrypt hashes, hashed tokens, every tenant's data) plus both volumes to ./backups on the host, with no encryption and no off-host copy. Recommendation: support encrypting bundles and pushing them off-host; REQ-88 documents the managed-platform split.

artifacts.title: SEC-13 CORS reflects any origin with credentials when configured as wildcard
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: both, only when misconfigured. cmd/server/main.go:636-640 reflects the caller's Origin and sets Allow-Credentials true whenever CORS_ORIGIN is "*". Production is configured with the exact frontend origin and a foreign origin received no CORS headers on 2026-09-06, so this is a latent footgun rather than a live exposure. Recommendation: REQ-100.

artifacts.title: SEC-14 Production metrics endpoint is open
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: Railway production (configuration). GET /metrics on openv-production.up.railway.app returned 61 KB of Prometheus output to an unauthenticated client on 2026-09-06: Go runtime statistics, request counts and latency per route template, run lifecycle gauges. Nothing tenant-specific leaks, but it maps the API surface and its load for anyone. The gate exists (OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN) and is simply not set on the Railway service. Recommendation: set OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN on the OpenV service, or restrict the path at the edge.

artifacts.title: SEC-15 Open, unverified self-registration on production
artifacts.body: Severity: Medium on Railway, Low self-hosted. POST /api/v1/auth/register is open on production with no email verification, no invitation and no throttling (SEC-5). Anyone can create accounts and personal workspaces, read and report the shared demo-product pool, and consume database and storage; with a paired runner of their own they can also drive the agent surface. Whether that is intended for a public instance is a product decision, but there is no way to close it today. Recommendation: REQ-95.

artifacts.title: SEC-16 Sessions live 30 days with no idle expiry or password-change invalidation
artifacts.body: Severity: Low. Affects: both. users.SessionDuration is 30 days (internal/domain/users/users.go:25) with no idle timeout; sessions are invalidated on logout and swept on expiry, but nothing invalidates other sessions when a password changes. A stolen cookie is therefore usable for up to a month. Recommendation: REQ-99.

artifacts.title: Tenant isolation
artifacts.body: No user, worker or agent shall read or write data belonging to a workspace they are not a member of.

artifacts.title: Personal runner scoping
artifacts.body: A personal runner shall claim only runs launched by its owning member.

artifacts.title: Hosted repo exclusion
artifacts.body: Hosted runners shall refuse runs requiring repository access; such runs shall wait for a personal or workspace runner.

artifacts.title: Hashed credentials, shown once
artifacts.body: Worker keys, agent run tokens and pairing codes shall be stored as sha256 hashes with plaintext revealed exactly once at creation.

artifacts.title: Untrusted content isolation in agent prompts
artifacts.body: A prompt the platform builds for a member's own assistant shall state up front that the product profile, wizard state, transcript and any artifact supplied for context are content and never instructions, and shall fence the state block and the artifact block, so that text authored in another tenant — a rolled community product seeds the wizard — or written into an artifact by anyone who can edit the project cannot read as an order to an agent running on the member's own machine with their credentials.

artifacts.title: Leased runner state erasure
artifacts.body: The system shall revoke a lease's credential when the lease ends. The leased runner shall erase that lease's vendor CLI credentials and working files before the runner serves another member.

artifacts.title: Runner pool credential scope
artifacts.body: The system shall restrict a runner pool node's own credential to the pool registration, heartbeat and release endpoints. The system shall grant a pool node access to a workspace's data only through the credential of a lease held by a member of that workspace.

artifacts.title: Throttling of authentication and launch endpoints
artifacts.body: The system shall throttle password sign-in and registration per client address and per account, so that a client that fails sign-in more than a configurable number of times in a window receives a rate-limited response until the window passes. The system shall throttle single sign-on callbacks and run launches per client address on the same terms. The limits shall key on the real client address when the operator declares a trusted proxy and on the connection address otherwise.

artifacts.title: Tool allowlists for agents that read untrusted content
artifacts.body: The runner shall start every vendor CLI with an explicit tool allowlist taken from the agent definition, and shall refuse to start an agent whose definition carries none. An agent whose prompt carries content authored outside the workspace, such as the interviewer, an agent with repository access, or an agent granted web fetch, shall run without automatic approval of file edits or shell commands, and the seeded interviewer shall hold read-only tools plus the candidate-need recorder only. The runner shall pass the same allowlist to every vendor CLI in that vendor's own terms.

artifacts.title: Provider key environment names from a fixed catalog
artifacts.body: The system shall accept as a provider's key environment variable only a name from the platform's catalog for that provider, and shall reject any other name on write. The runner shall inject into an agent's environment only the variable the catalog names for the run's provider, so that a workspace setting can never cause a runner to read and expose an unrelated variable from its host.

artifacts.title: Upload limits and safe serving of attachments
artifacts.body: The system shall cap the size of an uploaded attachment and of every request body at operator-configurable limits and shall refuse a larger one before reading it in full. The system shall serve every attachment with a content type sniffed from its bytes rather than the one the uploader supplied, shall serve an SVG or any other script-capable format as a download rather than inline, and shall send a no-sniff header and a sandboxing content security policy on every attachment response.

artifacts.title: Browser security headers
artifacts.body: Every response from the API and from the frontend server shall carry a no-sniff header, a frame-denying header, and a referrer policy. Every response served over TLS shall carry a strict transport security header. The frontend shall carry a content security policy that permits scripts from its own origin only, without unsafe inline or unsafe eval, and that names the API origin as the only connect source. The frontend server configuration shall apply these headers on every location, including those that set their own caching headers.

artifacts.title: Registration policy
artifacts.body: An operator shall be able to close self-service registration, so that new accounts arrive only through an invitation from a workspace admin or through the configured single sign-on provider. While registration is open the system shall throttle it per client address. The system shall document, for each deployment option, whether registration is open.

artifacts.title: Hosted runner container hardening
artifacts.body: The hosted runner provisioner shall create each container with no new privileges, with every capability dropped, with a process count limit, and with memory and CPU caps, and shall attach it to a network that reaches the API and the provider endpoints only. The operator documentation shall state that mounting the host's container socket into the API grants the API control of the host, and shall present the transient runner pool as the alternative that needs no socket.

artifacts.title: Secrets absent from logs and default configuration
artifacts.body: The request log shall redact the token segment of a public interview or connector path so that a live token never reaches a log line. The API shall refuse to start with the development worker key or the development database password when it listens on a non-loopback address. The base compose file shall not publish the database port to the host. The API image shall run as a non-root user.

artifacts.title: Session lifetime and idle expiry
artifacts.body: A session shall expire after an operator-configurable absolute lifetime and after an operator-configurable idle period, and the system shall invalidate every session of an account when its password changes or the account is removed. The defaults shall be no longer than 30 days absolute and 7 days idle.

artifacts.title: Cross-origin policy refuses wildcard with credentials
artifacts.body: The API shall allow credentialed cross-origin requests from the single configured frontend origin only, and shall refuse to start when the configured origin is a wildcard, so that no deployment can reflect an arbitrary origin together with credentials.

artifacts.title: Dependency vulnerability scanning in CI
artifacts.body: The continuous integration pipeline shall run a Go vulnerability check over the server and worker binaries and an audit of the frontend's production dependencies on every pull request, and shall fail the run on a reachable vulnerability of high severity or above.

artifacts.title: MCP stdio tool server
artifacts.body: Hand-rolled JSON-RPC MCP server (29 tools as of 2026-09-06) is the only data path between agents and OpenV: requirements, links, V&V evidence, coverage and gaps, baselines, kanban, proposals, quality rules, the project map and context bundles. Runs over stdio beside the agent CLI, authenticating with the run token agentd injects, or - for sessions that are not a platform-launched run, such as an agent maintaining this project - a workspace runner key from the environment. Enforces the lean-context rule by construction.

artifacts.title: Server-side proposal diversion
artifacts.body: Write endpoints detect an agent run context and divert mutations into proposal records; approval replays the operation as the reviewing human.

artifacts.title: agent_runs queue with routing claims
artifacts.body: The agent_runs table is the job queue (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). Claim SQL scopes personal keys to their owner's runs and holds reserved runs until hosted_after expires.

artifacts.title: agentd host worker with CLI adapters
artifacts.body: agentd polls for runs and drives claude/codex/gemini CLIs with openv-mcp wired in; interactive vendor sign-in is brokered to a visible console on the member's machine.

artifacts.title: Hosted runner provisioner and token-mode image
artifacts.body: Docker provisioner creates one openv-worker container per workspace; provider keys enter as container env at provision only; the image runs CLIs headless in API-key mode and claims with repo-access excluded.

artifacts.title: OpenV Agent Connector
artifacts.body: openv-connector:// protocol app: self-registers per-user, exchanges one-time pairing codes for the member's personal runner key, and starts agentd in its own console window. No service registration of any kind.

artifacts.title: Workspace authorization ladder
artifacts.body: Request authorization resolves platform admin, org admin, direct and team project grants, run-own-project and worker-same-org in one ladder; workers carry org and optional user scope from their key.

artifacts.title: Crew builder UIs
artifacts.body: Cytoscape-based org-chart editor with department containers and hierarchical layout, plus a network-diagram editor with typed edges; both edit the same crew graph.

artifacts.title: Shared products service and cross-tenant tables
artifacts.body: internal/domain/sharedproducts plus migration 0021 (shared_products, shared_product_reports). Sanitize-on-write flattens every field to inert single-line text; publication is gated to session principals, deduplicated by normalized name, and bounded by a per-workspace daily limit and a global pool ceiling, both env-tunable (OPENV_SHARED_PRODUCT_DAILY_LIMIT, OPENV_SHARED_PRODUCT_POOL_LIMIT). Distinct-reporter counting hides an entry at three. Neither table carries a foreign key to organizations: community content outlives the workspace that published it, and a workspace purge must not retract other people's roll list.

artifacts.title: artifacts.SectionNumbers document-order numbering
artifacts.body: A pure function over a project's live artifacts that walks the tree in document order (sort order, then creation time, then ID, so equal sort orders still number deterministically) and issues hierarchical numbers to headings only. A dangling parent is treated as a root and a parent cycle terminates, so a broken tree still numbers. The list handler exposes it behind doc_numbers=1 and reads the whole project to serve it, because a page or a type filter is a slice through the tree and cannot be numbered on its own.

artifacts.title: Invention quality gate
artifacts.body: describeProductFlaws enforces the invariants the built-in concepts already meet — the name riffs on the gimmick rather than bolting a suffix onto an unrelated product, the vision carries the name, the description is one mechanism in the 'A <what> that <what it does>.' shape, the audience is a qualified clause rather than a demographic, and the problem never names the product — phrased in the words the retry quotes back to the agent. A weak reply buys one retry; anything still below the bar is kept locally but never published.

artifacts.title: Remote MCP transport
artifacts.body: Proposed, not built: an HTTP MCP transport placed in front of the existing exported tool table, so the remote endpoint and the stdio server run the same handlers and no second tool implementation appears. Member-level authorization and per-client consent replace the bearer credential the stdio server takes from its environment.

artifacts.title: Layered quality rule sets
artifacts.body: A settings JSONB column on organizations and projects holds a rule set under one key, resolved defaults → workspace → project so each level stores only its own diff. The linter keeps one pattern set per convention and takes the resolved set as an argument, so it stays pure and a report can carry the rules that produced it. Unknown conventions, rules and severities are dropped on read and refused on write, and a settings read failure degrades to the platform defaults rather than failing the report. Agents receive the same resolved set through the tool surface and as a House style line in the AI map header.

artifacts.title: Server-side event name resolution
artifacts.body: The events endpoint decorates each stored event with an actor kind, the identifier inside the actor string and the display names behind it, plus the kind and name of the affected entity. Resolution runs only over the events that survive the project-visibility filter, so no identifier the caller may not see is ever dereferenced. Names come from the payload the publishing handler stamped in where it has one and from a repository lookup otherwise, memoized per page so a repeated actor, agent or artifact costs a single query. Every lookup is nil-safe and failure-tolerant: an unresolvable name is omitted and the client falls back to the raw identifier it still receives.

artifacts.title: Runner pool and lease protocol
artifacts.body: Pre-warmed agentd processes register against a deployment-wide pool key and heartbeat; a lease atomically reserves one idle node (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and mints a session-scoped personal runner key handed to the node once, on the heartbeat that picks the lease up. A server-side sweep ends lapsed leases (hard expiry, idle window, lost node) and revokes their keys. Needs no Docker daemon at the API, so it runs on platforms that offer replicas but no docker socket.

artifacts.title: Headless CLI sign-in relay
artifacts.body: A leased runner has no console and no browser, so each vendor flow is relayed through the existing login broker: TUI sign-ins (claude setup-token) run over a pseudo-terminal with a wide window so the URL does not soft-wrap, and the pasted code is typed back into it; loopback sign-ins (codex) have their redirect pasted back and replayed against the CLI's own advertised local port, using only the pasted path and query so another host cannot be reached.

artifacts.title: Browser hardening headers on API and frontend
artifacts.body: internal/api/security_headers.go stamps X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin and a default-src 'none' content security policy on every API response, plus Strict-Transport-Security when SECURE_COOKIES or CROSS_SITE_COOKIES declares a TLS-only deployment. The frontend's headers live in frontend/security-headers.conf, included in the nginx server block and again in every location that adds its own header, because nginx discards inherited add_header directives there. The frontend CSP permits scripts from the app's origin only (CRA's runtime chunk is built as a file with INLINE_RUNTIME_CHUNK=false and the theme bootstrap is public/theme-init.js), style-src 'self' plus inline styles for React, images from self, data, blob and the API origin, and connect-src self plus the API origin; the Docker build substitutes REACT_APP_API_URL into the policy and runs nginx -t so a broken configuration fails the image build.

artifacts.title: Credential endpoint throttling
artifacts.body: The token-bucket limiter already guarding the public interview routes (internal/api/ratelimit.go) now also guards the credential endpoints. Sign-in charges every attempt against the client address (OPENV_AUTH_IP_BURST 30, 120 per hour) and only a failed attempt against the normalised account email (OPENV_AUTH_ACCOUNT_BURST 5, 20 per hour), using a check-then-penalize pair so a correct password never spends the account's budget; registration charges per address (5, 10 per hour); the Google and OIDC start and callback routes charge per address (20, 60 per hour). A throttled request is answered 429 with Retry-After. Buckets are in-memory and per API instance, keyed on the real client address only when OPENV_TRUST_PROXY=1. Run launches are not yet throttled.

artifacts.title: Provider key variable catalog
artifacts.body: providers.AllowedAPIKeyEnvs fixes the environment variable names a provider setting may carry as api_key_env to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY, or blank for the provider's default. providers.Upsert refuses any other name with ErrInvalidSetting (a 400 at the API), and the runner (internal/runner/worker.go) independently refuses to start a run whose claim names a variable outside the catalog, failing the run with a configuration error, so a row written before the rule or a hostile API cannot turn a runner into a reader of its host's secrets.

artifacts.title: Request caps, upload sniffing and sandboxed SVG downloads
artifacts.body: api.BodyLimitMiddleware wraps every request body in http.MaxBytesReader at OPENV_MAX_BODY_MB (32 MB); attachment uploads read through io.LimitReader at OPENV_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (25 MB) and answer 413 beyond it (internal/api/attachment_safety.go). uploadLooksLikeImage checks the leading bytes against the declared type: raster formats through http.DetectContentType, TIFF by magic number, and SVG by an svg or xml root in text that sniffs as XML or plain text; a mismatch is a 400. Downloads carry nosniff; an SVG is served with Content-Disposition attachment and a CSP of sandbox; default-src 'none', so it never renders as a document on the API origin, while raster images stay inline with an img-src 'self' policy.

artifacts.title: CORS wildcard refusal
artifacts.body: api.CORSMiddleware replaces the inline handler in cmd/server/main.go. It returns ErrCORSOriginNotAllowed for an empty, "*" or "null" CORS_ORIGIN and the server refuses to start, so no deployment can reflect an arbitrary Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. A matching origin receives the credentialed allow headers and Vary: Origin; any other origin receives none and a foreign preflight is answered 200 without them.

artifacts.title: Request-log token redaction
artifacts.body: RequestLogMiddleware logs redactPath(r.URL.Path): for any path under /api/v1/public/interviews/ the invite-token segment is replaced with [token] before the line is written, so a live invite never reaches the access log or whatever aggregates it. Other paths are logged unchanged. Covers the log half of REQ-97; the development-default refusal and non-root API image remain open.

artifacts.title: Same-origin API proxy in the frontend image
artifacts.body: Built (PR #299, Phase 0 of the mobile plan). The frontend's nginx proxies `^~ /api/` to the API. The upstream address (`API_UPSTREAM`: the API service's Railway private domain on port 8080, or `api:8080` in compose) and the container's nameservers are written into `/etc/nginx/openv/api-proxy.conf` at container start by `frontend/docker-entrypoint.d/40-openv-api-proxy.sh`; the upstream is proxied through a variable so nginx re-resolves the name through DNS on every request instead of pinning a private address that changes on each API redeploy. Server-sent events and downloads stream unbuffered with a one-hour read timeout; `client_max_body_size 32m` matches the API's body cap; X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto (from the edge when present) and Host are forwarded; the location adds no frontend security headers because the API sets its own. Production builds leave `REACT_APP_API_URL` empty and the client defaults to a relative `/api` on its own origin; the content security policy's connect-src and img-src collapse to 'self'. The session cookie is then a first-party `SameSite=Lax` cookie, `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` comes off, and CORS is never exercised. For the remaining split deployments the API sets the `Partitioned` attribute on the session and OIDC cookies whenever `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` is on. The 27 MB connector download goes through the proxy unbuffered, so it needed no special case. Verified locally with a real nginx against a fake upstream: routing (including `^~` precedence over the asset regex for paths such as `/api/v1/attachments/x.png`), forwarded headers, unbuffered streaming, and a 413 above 32 MB. Deployment: `API_UPSTREAM` on the frontend service; `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` removed and `PUBLIC_URL` on the frontend origin for the API (docs/railway.md).

artifacts.title: Responsive shell: viewport classes, drawer navigation and stacked panes
artifacts.body: Built (PR #299, Phase 1 of the mobile plan). `frontend/src/hooks/viewport.ts` defines two breakpoints, phone (width ≤ 640 px) and tablet (≤ 900 px), and `useViewport` reports the class, `isPhone`, `isCompact` (phone or tablet) and `coarsePointer` (the `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` media query), kept current across resizes and orientation changes. Components that change shape read it once: ProjectLayout renders a top bar with a 48 px menu button below the tablet breakpoint and the navigation as a drawer over the page (closing on navigation, backdrop tap and Escape); on touch screens auto-hide panels behave as hidden and the edge strips widen to 24 px. ModuleView stacks into one pane at a time (Tree, Document, Notes) behind a segmented control; selecting an artifact moves to its document; panes are hidden rather than unmounted so tree state and editor drafts survive. GuidedWizard's StepShell replaces the 220 px rail with a progress strip and a native step picker; the V&V Assistant becomes a bottom sheet behind a floating button and stays mounted while closed. Global CSS: fields are 16 px on coarse pointers (no iOS focus zoom), the shell is 100dvh with a 100vh fallback, every table sits in an overflow-x wrapper, safe-area helpers and a reduced-motion rule; index.html declares viewport-fit=cover and the installed-app meta tags. Login, the create-workspace modal, the work-item drawer, the project-list navbar and the search popover no longer assume a desktop width; the help button moves bottom-left on phones. Verified by rendering the production build on Pixel 5 (Chromium) and iPhone 13 (WebKit) emulation with a mocked API, and by the mobile Playwright journey (TC-50).

artifacts.title: Touch parity: visible actions, Move to… dialog, pointer drag and board action sheet
artifacts.body: Built (PR #299, Phases 2 and 3 of the mobile plan). ArtifactList gives every row a visible ⋯ actions button that opens the same menu as right-click, positioned to stay on screen; the menu gains *Move to…*, a dialog that picks a target artifact from a native select in document order and a placement (before, after, inside), each option enabled only where `planMove` would accept the drop, and then calls the same reorder as a drop. On coarse pointers a grip handle drags rows through pointer events: `touch-action: none` is set on the handle alone so the rest of the list still scrolls by finger; the row under the pointer is found with `elementFromPoint` on `data-artifact-row` markers, the drop zone and feedback are the ones the HTML5 drag uses, and the list auto-scrolls near its edges. Up/down and menu targets are 44 px on touch. KanbanBoard on phones shows one column at a time with previous/next buttons and a segmented column picker; each card's ⋯ opens an actions sheet with *Open card* and *Move to <column>*, which performs the same move as a drop (so a card moved to To Do launches its agent exactly as a drag would); a locked card (agent run in progress) keeps its moves disabled. ReviewQueue renders suspect links as cards with 44 px controls on phones. The notifications panel spans the screen below the top bar on phones. Muted text is raised to 4.6:1 contrast and the manifest gains shortcuts and categories.

artifacts.title: Authorization matrix suite
artifacts.body: Automated Go suite exercising the role ladder: platform admin, org admin, direct grants, team grants, run-own-project, worker org scoping. Pass = every matrix cell returns the expected allow/deny.

artifacts.title: Tenant isolation end-to-end
artifacts.body: Live check with two accounts in different orgs: all cross-org reads and writes return 403/404; org directories and worker keys stay scoped; team-grant escalation raises effective role as designed.

artifacts.title: Personal key rotation suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite: minting a new personal key revokes the previous one; revoked keys fail resolution; each member holds at most one active personal key per workspace.

artifacts.title: Hosted token-mode smoke test
artifacts.body: openv-worker image boots with an API key env, reports the CLI logged in via API-key mode without any interactive login, and excludes repo-access runs from its claims.

artifacts.title: Copilot prompt isolation test
artifacts.body: The assistant prompt declares the product profile, wizard state, transcript and the artifact on screen as content and never as instructions, fences the state block and the artifact block, and places the trust rules ahead of every scrap of that content.

artifacts.title: Lease teardown and credential scope suite
artifacts.body: Ending a lease revokes its credential and sends the node to draining before it is released; a stale release from a finished lease cannot free a node that has since been leased again; a session key never displaces the member's own connector key while still counting as their runner for routing. The pool key authenticates a pool node and carries no workspace, user or worker identity, and a wrong key is rejected; the pool endpoints refuse a member session and a workspace worker key. End to end against a live API and pool node: after the lease ends the node's per-lease home is removed, the key is revoked, and a second lease on the same node reports the vendor CLI as installed but signed out.

artifacts.title: Production hardening probe
artifacts.body: Manual, against the deployed API and frontend with an unauthenticated HTTP client. 1. Send eight failed password sign-ins within two seconds from one address; expect a rate-limited response before the eighth. 2. Request the frontend root, a static asset and an API response; expect nosniff, a frame-denying header, a referrer policy and strict transport security on each, and a content security policy without unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval on the frontend. 3. Send a preflight and a plain request with a foreign Origin; expect no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. 4. Request /metrics without credentials; expect 401 when a metrics token is configured. 5. Post an empty registration; expect a validation error, and confirm whether registration is open for the deployment.

artifacts.title: Hardening middleware and credential throttle suite
artifacts.body: Go suites in internal/api and internal/domain/providers: every response carries nosniff, a frame-denying header, a referrer policy and a CSP, with HSTS only when the deployment declares TLS; a wildcard, empty or null CORS origin is refused at construction and only the configured origin receives credentialed allow headers, a foreign preflight receiving none; an oversized body is cut off with a MaxBytesError; an upload over the cap is answered 413 and a small one read whole; PNG bytes pass as PNG, HTML bytes fail as PNG or SVG, an SVG root or XML prolog passes as SVG, TIFF passes by magic number only; an SVG is served as an attachment inside a sandbox CSP and a raster image inline with img-src self; three wrong passwords close an account so both a wrong and a right password are then refused with 429 and Retry-After while another account from the same address still signs in; correct sign-ins never charge the account; an address is throttled across accounts; a second registration from one address is refused; nil throttles allow everything; the invite-token segment of public interview paths is redacted and other paths are left alone; a provider setting naming a variable outside the key catalog is refused and never persisted while every catalogued name and blank are accepted, and every provider's default variable is in the catalog.

artifacts.title: Requirements gap analysis 2026-09-06
artifacts.body:
Scope: the live **OpenV Platform** project (64 requirements, 11 needs,
16 design items, 33 test cases, baseline *2026-09-04 One download, chosen
and filtered*) challenged in its entirety against the feature set actually
shipped on `master` at `cfabf06` (Railway `release` at the same head).

Method: a route-by-route, package-by-package inventory of the codebase
(≈265 HTTP routes, 36 domain packages, 23 schema migrations, 21 SPA views,
5 Playwright journeys, 29 MCP tools) was compared with every requirement
body, every need, and every test case's evidence claim. Findings are graded:

| Grade | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **G1 — shipped, unspecified** | A capability exists with no requirement stating it. It cannot be traced, baselined or verified. |
| **G2 — specified, stale** | The requirement text no longer matches the platform. |
| **G3 — specified, unverified** | A requirement whose test case does not exist, does not do what it claims, or whose verification is missing. |
| **G4 — specified, not built** | A requirement stated as binding for something that is not implemented. |
| **G5 — need under-served** | A stakeholder need whose derived requirements do not cover how the platform actually serves it. |

Every finding below has been recorded in the live project (new draft
artifacts, edits, comments and links) so the project itself carries the
result; this file is the off-instance record. See "How the result was
recorded" at the end.

## 1. Summary

| Grade | Count | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| G1 shipped, unspecified | 19 capability groups | 25 new draft requirements (REQ-65 … REQ-89) + 14 new test cases (TC-34 … TC-47) added to the project |
| G2 stale | 6 | 4 requirement/design bodies updated; 2 tensions left as comments for the maintainer |
| G3 unverified | 18 requirements without a verifying test case; 1 test case overclaiming | Recorded as comments; 3 new test cases cover 4 of them |
| G4 not built | 2 (REQ-44 remote MCP; macOS connector in REQ-32) | Commented; REQ-44 left draft as a roadmap requirement |
| G5 need under-served | 3 needs (NEED-5, NEED-9, NEED-7 audit) | New requirements derive from them |

The requirement set is **strong where the last four weeks of work landed**
(figures, downloads, quality rules, runner leasing, agent seeds) and **thin
where the platform grew earlier and quietly**: the review workflow, baseline
comparison, impact analysis, search, notifications, budgets, run resilience,
import/templates, observability and backups are all shipped and untraced.
Security is specified by five requirements and verified by six test cases; the
companion security assessment records what those leave uncovered.

## 2. G1 — shipped but unspecified

Each row is a capability found in the code with no requirement stating it.
The "recorded as" column is the artifact created in the live project.

| # | Capability (evidence) | Under | Recorded as |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Artifact status workflow** — draft → in_review → approved → superseded, validated transitions, `PUT /artifacts/{id}/status`; approval clears link suspicion (`internal/domain/artifacts/status.go`) | HDG-3 | REQ-65 |
| 2 | **Suspect links and the review queue** — editing either end of a link flags it suspect until a reviewer confirms it (`PUT /links/{id}/confirm`); `/projects/{id}/review-queue` lists suspect links and in-review artifacts (migration 5, `ReviewQueue.tsx`, `e2e/tests/review-queue.spec.ts`) | HDG-3 | REQ-66; TC-34 |
| 3 | **Baseline comparison** — `GET /baselines/{id}/diff` against another baseline or live, Added/Modified/Removed with field flags (`internal/domain/baselines/diff.go`, `BaselineCompare.tsx`, `e2e/tests/baseline-diff.spec.ts`) | HDG-3 | REQ-67; TC-35 |
| 4 | **Impact analysis** — upstream/downstream/both traversal over links, depth-capped at 25 (`internal/domain/vv/impact.go`, `ImpactView.tsx`) | HDG-5 | REQ-73; TC-45 |
| 5 | **Search** — trigram search across a workspace (`/api/v1/search`, migration 9), opt-in semantic search and duplicate-candidate detection over pgvector embeddings, env-gated and off by default (`internal/domain/embeddings`, migration 16, `/projects/{id}/duplicates`, `/reindex-embeddings`) | HDG-3 | REQ-68, REQ-69; TC-36, TC-37 |
| 6 | **Typed attribute definitions** — org- and project-scoped definitions (enum/date/number/text) validated into artifact attributes (`internal/domain/attributes`, migration 15) | HDG-3 | REQ-70; TC-38 |
| 7 | **Project import and templates** — JSON and ReqIF import with remapped ids, drafts stamped; save-as-template and create-from-template (`internal/domain/exports/reqif_import.go`, `internal/domain/templates`) | HDG-3 | REQ-71, REQ-72; TC-39 |
| 8 | **Notifications** — in-app rows, live SSE push, per-user email opt-out, opt-in SMTP for high-signal types (`internal/notify`, migrations 6 and 13) | HDG-7 | REQ-78; TC-44 |
| 9 | **Budgets, plans and limits** — monthly budget per workspace with 80 %/100 % admin alerts, optional launch enforcement, `free`/`team` plan defaults for runner limits, month-to-date usage endpoint (`internal/notify/budgets.go`, `internal/domain/orgs/limits.go`) | HDG-6 | REQ-76, REQ-77; TC-44, TC-47 |
| 10 | **Run resilience** — failure taxonomy with a retryable subset, automatic retry chain capped by `OPENV_RUN_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, manual retry with provenance, stale-heartbeat reaper, cancel and release semantics, reproducibility snapshot per run (migrations 3, 12, 14; `internal/domain/agentruns/service_test.go`) | HDG-8 | REQ-84, REQ-85; TC-40 |
| 11 | **Proposal review at scale** — bulk approve/reject, 100-proposal cap per run, temporary ref tokens so one run can propose an artifact and a link to it (`/proposals/bulk`, migration 17) | HDG-7 | REQ-79; TC-40, TC-41 |
| 12 | **Crew templates, clone, export/import** — two built-in templates, crew clone, crew export/import across workspaces (`internal/domain/crewtemplates`, `/crews/{id}/export`, `/crews/import`) | HDG-7 | REQ-80; TC-42 |
| 13 | **Agent-executed test runs** — "Run N with agent" builds an instruction naming automated cases only; `manual`/`physical` cases are withheld and any agent result for them is refused (403); agent results carry a marker. "Draft test cases" launches the seeded test-case-author agent in proposal mode (`docs/agents.md`, `/test-runs/{id}/agent-run`, `/projects/{id}/draft-test-cases`) | HDG-5 | REQ-74, REQ-75; TC-45 |
| 14 | **Kanban-driven runs** — moving a card into an agent column enqueues a run; run progress lands on the card's activity (`internal/orchestration/hooks.go`) | HDG-7 | REQ-81 |
| 15 | **Agent configuration surface** — provider, model from a catalog or custom, reasoning effort, `allowed_tools` allowlist, `max_turns`, timeouts; provider settings with worker-reported detection (`internal/domain/providers`, `docs/agents.md`) | HDG-7 | REQ-82 |
| 16 | **AI context surface** — stable refs on every artifact, `get_project_map` (and `/projects/{id}/ai-map`), release-stamped maps by baseline, `get_context` bundles (`internal/api/ai_map.go`, `internal/mcp/context_bundle.go`) | HDG-7 | REQ-83; TC-46 |
| 17 | **Repository connections** — per-project connections, per-member local checkout paths, leased runners cloning by URL, hosted runners refusing (`internal/domain/repoconns`, `internal/runner/workspace.go`) | HDG-8 | REQ-86 (decomposed from REQ-25) |
| 18 | **Observability** — Prometheus `/metrics` with bounded cardinality and an optional bearer gate, structured request log annotated with the resolved actor, `/health` (`internal/metrics`, `internal/api/requestlog.go`) | HDG-17 Operations (new, under HDG-11) | REQ-87; TC-47 |
| 19 | **Backup, restore and schema migration** — `make backup`/`restore`, opt-in scheduled sidecar with retention, numbered migration ledger applied once under a boot advisory lock (`scripts/backup.sh`, `internal/persistence/postgres/migrations.go`) | HDG-17 Operations | REQ-88, REQ-89; TC-47 |

Also shipped and unspecified, recorded as one requirement each or folded into
the rows above: generic OIDC sign-in (folded into REQ-18), interview persona
linking and invite expiry/revocation (folded into REQ-8), the in-app manual
and contextual help, the global search box, theme switching, workspace member
self-removal, and the Usage tab.

## 3. G2 — stale requirements

| Ref | What is stale | Action taken |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-18 Authentication | Says email/password and Google only. The platform also offers **generic OIDC** (`OPENV_OIDC_*`, `oidc_handlers.go`) and refuses cross-provider sign-in for one email (`users_test.go`). | Body updated. |
| REQ-2 Typed artifacts | Lists eight types; the catalog has nine (**other**). Says "free-form attributes"; attributes can now be typed and validated (see G1 #6). | Body updated to name all nine types and reference typed definitions. |
| REQ-3 Semantically constrained links | Lists six link types; the rule set enforces eight (**impacts**, **relates-to** are unconstrained-by-type and bidirectional respectively). | Body updated. |
| DES-1 MCP stdio tool server | Says 27 tools; `internal/mcp/tools.go` exports 29. | Body updated. |
| REQ-21 Proposal-gated writes | "**All** agent-initiated changes shall be diverted into proposals" — but `write_mode: direct` exists by design, and a workspace runner key carries no gating (REQ-42 says so). The absolute wording contradicts two other requirements. | Comment left; recommended rewording: proposal mode is the default, direct mode is an explicit per-agent choice by a workspace admin. |
| REQ-20 Lean agent context | "shall not feed agents large prompt contexts or requirement documents" — REQ-41 and REQ-49 deliberately place the product profile, wizard state, transcript and the artifact on screen in the assistant prompt, and the V&V Assistant carries WebSearch/WebFetch. Not a contradiction in practice (the content is bounded and fenced) but the text reads as one. | Comment left; recommended rewording bounds what a prompt may carry rather than forbidding content outright. |
| REQ-53 / REQ-64 | Both specify the side-panel states; REQ-64 restates part of REQ-53 with a differing rule (a hidden panel opens on click, not hover). | Comment left; REQ-64 should `decomposes-to` from REQ-53 or the two should merge. |
| `docs/operations.md` | Says hosted-runner containers run with **no resource caps**; `docs/agents.md`, `docker-compose.prod.yml` and `internal/hosting/provisioner.go` apply memory/CPU caps from plan limits. | Doc fixed in this change. |

## 4. G3 — specified but unverified

Before this work `get_vv_gaps` reported **no gaps at all** while
`get_vv_coverage` listed nine requirements as *uncovered* (REQ-18, REQ-25,
REQ-35, REQ-36, REQ-44, REQ-51, REQ-53, REQ-54, REQ-58). The gap tool flags a
missing test case only for requirements whose method is `test`; a
`demonstration` or `analysis` requirement with no evidence and no
verification status is silent there while the coverage rollup calls it
uncovered. That disagreement between two V&V views of the same project is
itself a platform finding (REQ-12 says gaps are "actionable"; a requirement
the rollup calls uncovered should appear in them). Beyond it, two things were
hidden:

**Requirements with no verifying test case at all** (18): REQ-2, REQ-4,
REQ-5, REQ-13, REQ-14, REQ-18, REQ-19, REQ-20, REQ-22, REQ-23, REQ-24,
REQ-25, REQ-26, REQ-35, REQ-44, REQ-51, REQ-53, REQ-54. Most are
`demonstration`, which is legitimate for UI behaviour, but REQ-18, REQ-25
and REQ-44 carry no `verification_status` either, and REQ-26 (must,
verified) has only a design item behind it. New test cases now cover
REQ-5 and REQ-14 (TC-36 smoke journey), REQ-18 (TC-43) and REQ-22 (TC-42).

**A test case that overclaims**: TC-8 *Link rule validation suite* says
"Automated suite: each link type accepts its allowed from/to artifact types
and rejects all others". `internal/domain/links` has **no test files**; the
only coverage is indirect, in `internal/api/proposal_appliers_test.go`.
REQ-3 (must, method test) therefore has no direct evidence. Comment left on
TC-8.

**Evidence this session could produce**: the full Go suite passes
(`go test ./cmd/... ./internal/...`, 41 packages), which is the standing
evidence behind TC-1, TC-12, TC-14, TC-16, TC-17, TC-18, TC-20, TC-23,
TC-27, TC-28, TC-29 (unit half), TC-30 (automated half), TC-31 and TC-32.
Recorded as test run *2026-09-06 Assessment evidence* (29 results: 28 pass,
1 fail — the production hardening probe, see the security assessment). Not exercised here:
the Postgres-backed suites (skip without `OPENV_TEST_DATABASE_URL`), the
Playwright journeys and the client Jest suites (no built frontend in the
session), and every live check (TC-2, TC-5, TC-6, TC-7, TC-10, TC-11).

## 5. G4 — specified but not built

- **REQ-44 Remote MCP workspace connector** is written as "shall" but its own
  body ends "Not yet implemented"; DES-12 is "Proposed, not built". It should
  either carry a status the convention recognises (draft is right; it must
  not be approved or given a verification status) or move to a roadmap
  section. No test case exists; none should until it lands.
- **REQ-32 On-demand Agent Connector** promises "a single self-contained
  executable per OS"; `Dockerfile.api` builds Windows and Linux only, and
  `docs/railway.md` says macOS has no prebuilt download. Either the
  requirement names the two supported OSes or macOS is a known gap.

## 6. G5 — needs under-served by their requirements

- **NEED-9 Predictable agent execution** derives only REQ-27 and REQ-28
  (routing). The platform's actual answer to "starts reliably" is the retry
  chain, failure taxonomy and stale-run reaper (G1 #10) — now derived from
  NEED-9.
- **NEED-5 One view of human and AI work** derives only REQ-23. The
  notifications surface and board-driven runs (G1 #8, #14) are the other
  half of that view — now derived from NEED-5.
- **NEED-7 Audit-ready traceability** has no requirement for baseline
  comparison, impact analysis or the review queue (G1 #2, #3, #4) — the
  three features an auditor would actually use — now derived from NEED-7.

## 7. Conventions and hygiene observations

- The project's rule set is ISO 29148 "shall". 30 of the 64 requirements
  are `approved`; 34 are `draft`, including `must` requirements that have
  been verified for weeks (REQ-1, REQ-7, REQ-26, REQ-34, REQ-40, REQ-41…). A
  status pass would let the coverage rollup mean something.
- `priority` is unset on REQ-34 and REQ-35.
- The MoSCoW `priority` attribute and the body keyword are kept separate
  throughout, as the rule set requires.
- Test cases TC-31…TC-33 sit at the project root rather than under HDG-10 /
  HDG-14; moved under HDG-14 as part of this work.

## 8. How the result was recorded in the live project

1. New heading **HDG-16 Assessments** with two description artifacts holding
   this report and the security assessment.
2. New need **NEED-12 Run it myself without an operations team** (the
   operational and security requirements had no need to derive from).
3. New draft requirements REQ-65 … REQ-89 (G1) under the headings named in
   §2 and a new **HDG-17 Operations** heading, each with `derives-from` to
   the need it serves and `verifies` from a new test case (TC-34 … TC-47)
   where a suite exists. REQ-86 also `decomposes-to` from REQ-25.
4. Security: REQ-90 … REQ-100, HAZ-1 … HAZ-16 under **HDG-18 Security
   hazards**, and TC-48 — see the security assessment.
5. Body updates to REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-18 and DES-1 (G2); comments on REQ-20,
   REQ-21, REQ-32, REQ-44, REQ-53 and TC-8. TC-31 … TC-33 moved under
   HDG-14.
6. Test run **2026-09-06 Assessment evidence** with the Go-suite results and
   the production probe.
7. Baseline **2026-09-06 Requirements and security assessment**.
8. A fresh export under `docs/exports/`.

artifacts.title: Security assessment 2026-09-06
artifacts.body:
Authorised defensive review of OpenV at `master` `cfabf06` (the same head
Railway `release` is serving), covering both deployment options:

- **Self-hosted** — `docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.prod.yml`,
  `Dockerfile.api`, `Dockerfile.worker`, `frontend/Dockerfile.prod` +
  `frontend/nginx.conf`, the backup sidecar.
- **Railway production** — the `OpenV` (API), `OpenV Frontend`, `OpenV
  Runner Pool` and `Postgres` services in the `incredible-solace` project.

Method: the security model claimed in `docs/architecture.md` and
`docs/operations.md` was verified claim by claim in code; every HTTP route
was traced for authentication and authorisation; `govulncheck` and `npm
audit --omit=dev` were run; the full Go suite was run; and the live
production API and frontend were probed with an unauthenticated client
(headers, CORS, throttling, metrics, registration, body limits). The Railway
service configuration was read through the Railway API (variable names only,
never values). No file was modified and no production data was written
outside the OpenV Platform project.

## 1. Verdict

**No authentication bypass and no cross-tenant access was found in the HTTP
API.** The multi-tenant model is coherent and consistently applied: bcrypt
passwords, every token from `crypto/rand` and stored as SHA-256, one
authorisation ladder on essentially every handler, object-to-project
resolution before any check (no IDOR found), org-scoped worker keys, a
least-privilege pool key, OIDC with nonce and state binding, sanitised 5xx
responses, parameterised SQL throughout, no raw HTML in the SPA.

The findings cluster in three places:

1. **The agent execution surface.** Vendor CLIs run with auto-approved edits
   (Gemini) or workspace-write sandboxes without a tool allowlist (Codex),
   while their prompts carry text from interview participants, repositories
   and web pages. Proposal gating protects OpenV data; it does not protect
   the runner host. This is the one **High**.
2. **Production configuration and hardening that the code supports but the
   deployment does not apply**: no throttling on sign-in, no security
   headers reaching the browser (an nginx `add_header` inheritance rule
   silently discards them), an open `/metrics`, open self-registration.
3. **Hygiene**: default secrets on the base compose file, a root API image,
   unencrypted on-host backups, a known-vulnerable Docker client module,
   invite tokens in the access log.

Every finding is recorded in the OpenV Platform project as a hazard
(HAZ-1 … HAZ-16 under *Security hazards*), each pointing at the draft
requirement (REQ-90 … REQ-100) that would close it, so `get_vv_gaps` shows
them as unmitigated until a design item mitigates them. The production
probe is test case TC-48 with a recorded **fail** in the run *2026-09-06
Assessment evidence*.

## 2. Findings

| ID | Severity | Affects | Finding | Closes with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-1 | **High** | both | Prompt injection into auto-approving vendor CLIs. ## 3. Deployment-specific picture

### Railway production

| Aspect | State |
|---|---|
| Services | API, frontend, runner pool (1 replica each), Postgres; all online, no critical issues in the last 7 days; one failed pool deploy on 2026-09-05 since superseded. |
| Exposure | API and frontend have public domains; Postgres and the runner pool have none (private network only). |
| Variables (names only) | API: `CORS_ORIGIN`, `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES`, `DATABASE_URL`, `FRONTEND_URL`, `HOSTED_RUNNERS`, `OPENV_DATA_DIR`, `PUBLIC_URL`, `RUNNER_POOL_KEY`, `SECURE_COOKIES`, `UPLOADS_DIR`, `WORKER_API_KEY`. Not set: `OPENV_METRICS_TOKEN`, `OPENV_TRUST_PROXY`, any `OPENV_OIDC_*`/`GOOGLE_*`, `OPENV_SMTP_*`, `OPENV_EMBEDDING_*`. |
| Cookies | `SECURE_COOKIES` and `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` set — session cookie is `SameSite=None; Secure`, which the split-domain layout requires. |
| TLS | Terminated at Railway's edge (HTTP/2). No HSTS from the origin. |
| Database | `DATABASE_URL` carries `sslmode=disable` on the private network, as `docs/railway.md` prescribes. |
| Legacy key | `WORKER_API_KEY` is set. It is accepted raw by the middleware and maps to the bootstrap workspace; prefer minted workspace keys and remove it once no runner uses it. |
| Trust proxy | `OPENV_TRUST_PROXY` unset, so per-IP limits (interview routes today, sign-in tomorrow) key on Railway's edge address rather than the client's. Set it to `1` behind Railway. |
| Open | SEC-5, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15 are live on this deployment; SEC-1, SEC-3, SEC-6, SEC-9, SEC-16 apply in code. |

### Self-hosted (compose)

| Aspect | State |
|---|---|
| Prod overlay | Forces `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `CORS_ORIGIN`, `WORKER_API_KEY`; unpublishes 5432; healthchecks; memory limits; nginx unprivileged. Good. |
| Base file | Dev secrets and published 5432 (SEC-4). Running it on a reachable host is the risk. |
| Hosted runners | Require the Docker socket in the API container (root-equivalent host control); containers lack hardening beyond memory/CPU (SEC-2); `docker/docker` module vulnerable (SEC-7). Prefer the runner pool, which needs no socket. |

## 4. Controls verified as sound

- Passwords: bcrypt at default cost, minimum eight characters; SSO accounts
  bound to one provider, cross-provider sign-in refused, `email_verified`
  required.
- Tokens: worker keys, run tokens, pairing codes, invite tokens and session
  tokens are 32 random bytes, stored as SHA-256, shown once; env, pool and
  metrics keys compared in constant time.
- Authorisation: `requireProjectRole` / `requireOrgRole` / `requireRunAccess`
  applied on every non-public handler; every object addressed by id is
  resolved to its project or workspace first; workers cannot reach another
  org; pool key reaches pool endpoints only; run tokens scoped to one project
  and revoked at finish.
- OIDC: full ID-token verification, nonce replay binding, one-shot state
  cookie. Cookies `HttpOnly`, `Secure` under flag, correct `SameSite=None`
  pairing.
- Data: parameterised SQL throughout; LIKE escaped; cursor ids validated; git
  invoked by argv; agent slugs regex-validated with a path-escape check;
  attachment names sanitised (TC-23).
- Tenancy: search, events, SSE and notifications filtered to accessible
  projects / the authenticated user; shared products sanitised, session-only,
  attributable and removable (TC-14).
- Errors sanitised; no `InsecureSkipVerify`; connector refuses non-HTTPS
  pairing; provider settings store the key's env *name*, never the key;
  login records redacted; worker and frontend images non-root; base images
  pinned; CI promotion green-only with minimal permissions.
