artifacts.title: Bring-your-own-AI runners
artifacts.body: Each member shall be able to run agents through their own vendor CLI subscription, on their own machine (personal runner) or on a runner leased to that member alone (transient runner). The platform shall drive every consumer subscription through the vendor's own CLI, signed in by the member who owns it, and shall never share a member's subscription with another member, proxy its credentials, or execute it in the API server.

artifacts.title: First-refusal routing
artifacts.body: A run launched by a member with an online personal runner shall be reserved for that runner for a grace window (default 60 seconds, workspace-tunable) before hosted or workspace runners may claim it; ownerless runs shall route immediately.

artifacts.title: Token-only hosted runners
artifacts.body: Company-wide AI shall run in platform-provisioned hosted containers using org API tokens supplied as container environment at provision time only; provider keys shall never be stored.

artifacts.title: On-demand Agent Connector
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a downloadable Agent Connector as a single self-contained executable per OS that registers an openv-connector:// protocol handler, unpacks its runner components beside itself on first run, and starts the member's personal runner on demand from the browser. The connector shall remember one pairing per workspace (pairing a new workspace must not invalidate existing pairings) and shall start against the pairing of the workspace the browser requests.

artifacts.title: Credential-free pairing links
artifacts.body: The browser shall hand the connector a single open-or-pair link carrying the workspace and a one-time pairing code (10-minute TTL, single use). The connector shall use its existing pairing for that workspace when present and spend the code to pair only when it has none, so routine opens never rotate a working runner key; deliberate re-pairing (key rotation) remains an explicit action in workspace runner settings.

artifacts.title: Remote MCP workspace connector
artifacts.body:
The platform shall expose its tool surface over an authenticated remote MCP endpoint, so a member can attach a compliant AI client to their workspace without installing a local binary or holding a long-lived shared secret.

The endpoint shall reuse the platform's existing tool definitions and authorization rules, shall authenticate the member rather than a workspace-wide key, and shall record the member's consent per client. Not yet implemented: the local stdio path remains the supported route.

artifacts.title: Transient runner leasing
artifacts.body: The system shall lease one pre-warmed runner from its runner pool to a requesting member. The system shall reserve that runner for the leasing member alone. The system shall route runs that member launches to the leased runner on the same first-refusal terms as a personal runner. The member shall install no software to obtain or use the leased runner.

artifacts.title: Browser-relayed sign-in on a leased runner
artifacts.body: The system shall relay each vendor CLI sign-in that runs on a leased runner to the requesting member's browser. The system shall present the authorization link the CLI produces. The system shall accept the authorization code or redirect address the member returns.

artifacts.title: Runner lease expiry
artifacts.body: The system shall end a runner lease when the workspace's configured lease lifetime elapses. The system shall also end the lease when the leased runner claims no work within the workspace's configured idle window. Whichever condition occurs first shall end the lease, and the system shall record which one did.

artifacts.title: Run failure classification and retry
artifacts.body: The system shall classify every failed run as one of provider unavailable, authentication, workspace, timeout, agent error or worker error, and shall treat a defined subset of those classes as retryable. The system shall automatically enqueue a fresh attempt for a retryable failure of a top-level run, recording its provenance, until a configurable attempt cap is reached, and shall not auto-retry an orchestrated child run or when the operator disables auto-retry. A member shall be able to retry a terminal failed run by hand. The system shall fail a run whose heartbeat lapses and shall refuse a second terminal report for the same run. Cancelling a queued run shall cancel it atomically; cancelling a running run shall set a flag the runner honours at its next check.

artifacts.title: Run reproducibility snapshot
artifacts.body: At launch the system shall capture, on the run record, the agent definition, provider, model, effort, tool allowlist and prompt the run will execute with, so that a later reader can see exactly what a run was given even after the agent definition changes.

artifacts.title: Repository connections and per-member paths
artifacts.body: A project owner shall connect one or more code repositories to a project by URL, and each member shall record the local checkout path of that repository on their own machine. A personal runner shall operate on the member's local checkout; a leased runner shall clone the connection's URL because it holds no checkout; a hosted runner shall refuse the run. The system shall never store repository credentials.

artifacts.title: Coverage computation
artifacts.body: The system shall compute verification coverage of requirements (via verifies links) and validation coverage of user needs (via validates links), including latest test-run results.

artifacts.title: Traceability matrix
artifacts.body: The system shall present a traceability matrix relating needs, requirements and test cases.

artifacts.title: Gap reporting
artifacts.body: The system shall report unverified requirements, unvalidated needs and failing verifications as actionable gaps.

artifacts.title: Test run recording
artifacts.body: The system shall record test runs capturing pass/fail results per test case over time.

artifacts.title: Change impact analysis
artifacts.body: The system shall report the set of artifacts a change to a given artifact affects by traversing its traceability links upstream, downstream or in both directions, grouped by artifact type and annotated with the link path that reached each one. The system shall bound the traversal at a fixed depth so that a cyclic graph terminates.

artifacts.title: Agent-executed test runs
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor hand the automated test cases of a test run to an agent, and shall build the agent's instruction naming exactly those test cases. Each test case shall carry an execution method of automated, manual or physical. The system shall withhold manual and physical test cases from the agent's instruction and shall refuse, with a forbidden response, any result an agent run records against one. The system shall stamp every agent-recorded result with the run that produced it and shall show that provenance beside the result. A result applied from an approved proposal shall count as human-executed.

artifacts.title: Agent-drafted test cases
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor select requirements and launch the seeded test-case author agent against them. The agent shall run in proposal mode, so that every drafted test case and its verifies link reach the project only through human approval.

artifacts.title: Guided product definition wizard
artifacts.body: The system shall provide a step-by-step guided wizard (framing, personas, needs, requirements, NFRs, hazards, verification stubs, review) that materializes traceable draft artifacts as the user progresses. Hazards shall be captured under risk categories (Safety, Technical, Security, Programme, Operational) and non-functional requirements under quality attributes (Performance, Reliability, Usability, Security, Maintainability, Regulatory). Materialized artifacts shall be organized under automatically created section headings — one per wizard step, with a sub-heading per used NFR category, per used hazard category, and per verification grouping (Functional first, then each quality attribute stubbed) — reused across wizard re-runs within the same session. A category shall place an artifact in the document rather than appear as a prefix on its title, and a verification stub shall be filed beside the kind of requirement it verifies, carrying the same title as that requirement. A category the wizard no longer offers shall file its artifact directly under the step's own heading rather than create a section no step can refill. Once any guided session exists for a project, the wizard's navigation entry shall be hidden; the wizard is then reached only via the Product Overview page's adaptive control (Start / Resume / Modify guided definition).

artifacts.title: Interview invitation links
artifacts.body: Members shall be able to invite internal or external people by link to an interview session; invitees shall need no OpenV account.

artifacts.title: Conversational AI elicitation
artifacts.body: The interview session shall be an AI-led natural conversation that asks questions to understand what the invitee needs from the product, and shall record proposed artifacts as interview-tagged drafts for member review - never as directly approved content.

artifacts.title: Random test product generation
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall offer a testing mode that generates a random product concept (name, description, vision, problem statement, target users) across varied categories including software, hardware, games, toys, and appliances, with the option to reroll, and shall seed the guided definition wizard with the generated framing so the connected V&V Assistant can expand it into a full definition.

artifacts.title: Agent-invented demo products
artifacts.body: The new-project flow shall let a member invent a demo product with their own connected agent, briefed with worked examples and the invariants the built-in concepts hold to, and shall offer the result as a roll tagged as the agent's. A reply that misses those invariants shall buy one retry told exactly what to fix; anything still below the standard shall be shown to its inventor but kept out of the collection everyone rolls from. Inventions shall be kept in the browser and mixed into later rerolls.

artifacts.title: Shared demo-product pool
artifacts.body: The system shall maintain one community pool of demo products that every workspace reads and contributes to, so the roll list grows across tenants rather than going stale per browser; a roll shall mix built-in concepts, this browser's inventions and the pool, deduplicated so no product rolls twice as often as its neighbours. Reading shall require a session. Publishing shall require a signed-in person — agent run tokens and worker keys shall be refused — and an invention shall publish automatically under its inventor's own session, so every entry stays attributable to an account. Entries shall be flattened server-side to inert single-line text carrying no line breaks, backticks, angle brackets, links or agent-suggestion markers, capped per field, deduplicated by name, limited per workspace per day and capped in total. Responses shall carry no author identity.

artifacts.title: Community pool moderation and takedown
artifacts.body: Because nothing reviews a shared demo product before other tenants see it, the system shall let any signed-in user report an entry, shall hide an entry once three distinct people have reported it, and shall let a platform admin delete one outright; repeated reports from one account shall count once. Author identity shall be stored for rate limiting and takedown only. Before anyone shares, the wizard shall state that publication is public and permanent, that rolls tagged with the globe were written by other users, and that creating a project from a product never shares it.

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant across the wizard and artifact notes
artifacts.body:
The system shall provide one assistant, named the V&V Assistant, reachable both beside the guided definition wizard and in the Notes panel of the requirements module. One conversation shall serve a whole project, so that what a member asks in the wizard is present in the notes and the reverse. The Notes panel shall present the artifact's comments and the assistant as separate tabs, and shall offer the assistant whether or not an artifact is selected. With an artifact selected, that artifact shall be supplied to the turn as fenced untrusted content, so the assistant answers about what the reader has open and cites it by its stable reference. Suggestion cards shall be applicable only in the wizard, where the entry sections they fill exist. A session created solely to hold the conversation shall not count as a guided definition in progress, so that opening the notes chat neither removes the wizard from the project navigation nor offers to resume a definition nobody started.

A workspace provisioned before the assistant was named shall adopt the current name, description and system prompt for its seeded agent, field by field and only where the workspace still carries the text the previous seed wrote; a field a member has edited shall be left as they wrote it, and an agent already current shall not be rewritten. The agent's slug shall not change, so that a workspace provisioned before the rename keeps a working chat.

artifacts.title: Claim routing suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite plus live check: a personal key never claims another user's run; reserved runs return no-content to workspace workers during the grace window and are claimable after hosted_after expires; ownerless runs route immediately.

artifacts.title: Connector pairing end-to-end
artifacts.body: On a real host: pairing deep link opens the connector, the one-time code exchanges for a personal key (second use rejected, expiry enforced), config is saved, agentd starts and reports online; uninstall removes the protocol handler.

artifacts.title: Agent proposal loop end-to-end
artifacts.body: Live run: agent claims a run with a run token, submits an artifact change, the change lands as a pending proposal, human approval materializes the artifact with correct attribution.

artifacts.title: Link rule validation suite
artifacts.body: Automated suite: each link type accepts its allowed from/to artifact types and rejects all others with a descriptive error.

artifacts.title: V&V dashboard verification
artifacts.body: Coverage, traceability matrix and gap views render correct figures for a project with known links and test-run history.

artifacts.title: Interview elicitation flow
artifacts.body: An invited external user opens the interview link without an account, holds a conversation, and the resulting artifacts appear as interview-tagged drafts pending member review.

Covers the reporting surfaces; the detail heading, tree rows and traceability rows remain verified by demonstration.

artifacts.title: V&V Assistant notes chat suite

artifacts.title: Quality rules editor presentation

artifacts.title: Figure numbering and version suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over the figure reference rules: a reference formats and parses round-trip, a non-figure (an artifact reference, a zero or missing number, a filename) is refused, the stored filename is the figure's with the uploaded extension carried over, an upload with no usable extension gets none, and a hostile extension (quotes, backslashes, path traversal, percent escapes, an over-long tail) is stripped rather than carried into a filename or a Content-Disposition header. A new attachment starts at version one carrying no figure until the repository allocates one.

artifacts.title: Description reference suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the reference helpers: the offer lists an artifact's own figures before the artifacts it links to, excludes anything it is not linked to, follows a link in either direction and names each neighbour once, skips a neighbour with no reference to cite and figures belonging to other artifacts, and offers nothing while an artifact is still being created. The caret rules: a hash opens the offer only at a word boundary (so 'PR#12' and URL fragments are ignored), it closes once the writer moves past it, and it reads from the caret rather than the end of the text. Insertion replaces what was typed, keeps the text that followed, and leaves the caret after the reference.

artifacts.title: Artifact drag placement suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the drag helpers: the pointer's quadrant resolves to before/after/child and is read relative to the row rather than the page, a zero-height row does not divide by zero, an artifact is recognised as its own descendant to any depth, a cycle already in the data terminates the search rather than hanging, and a planned move places a sibling before or after, appends a child last, moves an artifact out to the root or between two different parents, and refuses a drop onto itself, into its own subtree, or one that changes nothing.

artifacts.title: Project menu group expansion suite
artifacts.body: Client suite over the helpers that decide which menu groups are open: an unchosen group is collapsed, the group holding the current page opens itself, an explicit choice beats both defaults, and one click closes a group that opened itself. The route helper reads the module out of a project path (including a deep path and the overview) and reports nothing outside the project. Stored choices round-trip through browser storage, and stored junk — unparseable text, an array, a non-boolean value — falls back to the default rather than breaking the menu.

artifacts.title: Download selection and archive suite
artifacts.body:
Go suite over the selection filter and the download assembly, plus the client suite over the form that drives them.

Selection: the whole project passes through untouched; headings drop out on request; a section brings its whole subtree including grandchildren; a type filter and a section filter combine; a link survives only when both of its ends do; attachment metadata always travels with its artifact while the files are opt-in; a parent cycle already in the data terminates rather than hanging; the snapshot handed in is never mutated.

Assembly: every format renders the same narrowed snapshot; the baseline's name reaches the renderer; a download with no attachment categories is the plain file; one with categories is a zip holding the document and the files; only the categories asked for are packed; an unreadable file is recorded in a manifest rather than failing the download; archive entry names cannot climb out of the archive; two files with one name both survive.

Options: sections, types and attachment categories are counted off the project, and a project with none offers none.

Client: everything ticked sends no filter, an unticked box sends the narrowing, the query carries a baseline but not the live project, and an empty selection is refused before it is sent.

artifacts.title: Runner lease lifecycle suite
artifacts.body: Domain and repository suites over the pool: leasing takes an idle node and mints one credential handed over exactly once; a second lease for the same member returns the first; a one-node pool refuses a second member; the atomic lease under eight concurrent callers gives four nodes to four callers and never the same node twice; the sweep ends leases past their hard expiry, past their idle window, stuck starting, and on nodes that stopped heartbeating, with the reason recorded on each; activity defers the idle timeout; extending is capped from the lease's start.

artifacts.title: Headless sign-in relay suite
artifacts.body: Automated: the loopback replay forwards the pasted path and query to the CLI's own advertised listener, ignores any host named in the paste, rejects a paste carrying no authorization code with a message naming what to paste, and reports a rejected replay rather than swallowing it; ANSI-painted terminal output is reduced to text the authorization URL can be scraped from. Manual, because it needs a real vendor subscription: start a user-targeted sign-in against a leased runner for each provider and confirm the authorization link reaches the browser, the pasted value completes the flow, and the provider is then reported signed in.

artifacts.title: Review queue journey and status suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over the status machine and suspect flagging (internal/domain/artifacts/status_test.go, suspect_test.go): every permitted transition is accepted, every other transition is refused, superseded is terminal, and a content change on either end flags a link suspect while an attribute-only change does not. Playwright journey (e2e/tests/review-queue.spec.ts): two requirements linked decomposes-to, the parent submitted for review, the child edited so the link turns suspect, the Review Queue lists both, and Confirm clears the suspect link.

artifacts.title: Baseline diff suite and journey
artifacts.body: Go suite over baselines.Diff (internal/domain/baselines/diff_test.go): added and removed artifacts, modified artifacts with per-field flags, links compared by ends and type so a recreated link is unchanged, a link whose artifact was removed still names it, nil entries ignored, sorted deterministic output. Playwright journey (e2e/tests/baseline-diff.spec.ts): capture a baseline, edit a title, and Compare shows the edit under Modified with the old and new value.

artifacts.title: Smoke journey
artifacts.body: Playwright journey (e2e/tests/smoke.spec.ts) against a running stack: register a fresh user and land in the personal workspace, create a project, create a requirement and a user need, link them derives-from, capture a baseline through the prompt dialog, move the requirement from draft to in review, find it through global search, and download the project as JSON through the download wizard.

artifacts.title: Embedding service suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over internal/domain/embeddings: the provider is disabled by default and enabled only by its environment, the service is a no-op without a provider or a store, an artifact is embedded when new, re-embedded on a content or model change and skipped when unchanged, empty content is skipped, a provider error propagates without failing the caller, a dimension mismatch disables the service, fan-out is bounded, and a project reindex embeds every artifact.

artifacts.title: Attribute definition suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over internal/domain/attributes: definition defaults and validation, project definitions overriding workspace ones of the same name, and value validation per type (text, number, date, enumeration) with wrong-typed and out-of-list values refused.

artifacts.title: Import and ReqIF suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over internal/domain/exports: a JSON export imports with every artifact at version one, imported artifacts can be stamped draft, garbage is rejected, ReqIF export is well formed with hierarchy and structure, a ReqIF document round-trips, a malformed ReqIF is refused, and an enumerated value outside its datatype is refused.

artifacts.title: Agent run lifecycle suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over internal/domain/agentruns (service_test.go): a retryable failure of a top-level run auto-retries until the attempt cap, a non-retryable class and an orchestrated child run do not, the opt-out is honoured, manual retry enqueues a fresh run with provenance and only for terminal failures, a stale heartbeat fails the run and auto-retries, a second terminal report is refused, finish and mark-running lose the race to the reaper cleanly, cancel of a queued run is atomic and of a running run sets the flag only, release returns a claimed run to the queue, launch captures the reproducibility snapshot, and a run with pending proposals awaits approval and finalises when they resolve.

artifacts.title: Proposal reference and applier suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over internal/domain/proposals and internal/api/proposal_appliers_test.go: a temporary reference is lifted from the payload, a duplicate reference in one run is refused, a link proposal resolves when its artifact proposal is approved first and fails when the artifact is rejected or approved after the link, a link without references passes through, resolution fires when the last proposal resolves, and appliers replay approved writes through the real services including link-type validation.

artifacts.title: Crew template suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over internal/domain/crewtemplates: the built-in templates have the expected shape and the founder template imports against the seeded agent slugs, serialisation drops human nodes, an export imports across workspaces and round-trips, a node whose slug is missing is skipped with its edges, and a document of the wrong kind or without a name is refused.

artifacts.title: Sign-in provider binding suite
artifacts.body: Go suite over internal/domain/users: a new single sign-on user records its provider, the same provider signs in again, a different provider for the same email is refused in both directions (Google then OIDC, and cross-provider generally), a password shorter than eight characters is refused, and the password hash verifies with bcrypt.

artifacts.title: Budget and notification fan-out suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over internal/notify: a budget alert reaches the workspace admins once at 80 percent, escalates once to 100 percent, can go straight to 100, and is a no-op below threshold or without a budget; a pending proposal fans out to editors, a failed run notifies only its launcher, a completed interview and an artifact in review notify editors, mentions reach the named members, the actor is never notified and automatic entries are skipped, a member-list failure is swallowed; the mailer is a no-op unconfigured, sends configured types over SMTP, honours the per-user opt-out and the type filter, and deep links mirror the bell.

artifacts.title: Impact traversal and execution method suite
artifacts.body: Go suites over internal/domain/vv: impact traversal upstream, downstream and both, grouped by type with the reaching path, terminating on cycles at the depth cap (impact_test.go); and the execution-method rules that keep manual and physical test cases out of an agent's instruction and refuse an agent-recorded result for one (execution_test.go).

artifacts.title: Seed adoption updates only unedited fields
artifacts.body:
Automated, `internal/seeds` (`TestAdoptSeedDefaults*`).

1. An agent holding a previous release's prompt and tools, with the current name and description, adopts the new prompt and the newly granted tools; a field the workspace owns (model) is left alone.

2. An auto-hiding panel opens on hover and closes without it.

The mobile journey: register on a phone-sized screen; create a project and land in the compact shell (menu button present, no permanent sidebar); open the drawer, expand a group and navigate, and see the drawer close on arrival; in the requirements module see the Tree / Document / Notes control, create a requirement from the tree pane, tap it and land on its document, switch to Notes and back with the tree state kept; return to the project list.
