artifacts.title: Lean agent context
artifacts.body: Agents shall obtain project requirements context exclusively from the requirements database and kanban card history via tools; the system shall not feed agents large prompt contexts or requirement documents.

artifacts.title: Solo Founder
artifacts.body: Defines and builds products end-to-end alone. Uses OpenV as product manager, requirements tool and virtual development team, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting under their review.

artifacts.title: Company Admin
artifacts.body: Owns a company workspace: manages members, teams, project access, workspace AI keys and the hosted runner. Accountable for tenant privacy and spend.

artifacts.title: Team Contributor
artifacts.body: Engineer or product person working in granted projects. Brings their own AI subscription via a personal runner; launches and reviews agent work.

artifacts.title: External Stakeholder
artifacts.body: Customer, domain expert or colleague invited by link to express needs in a natural conversation. Has no OpenV account and never sees the tool itself.

artifacts.title: GUI-editable agent definitions
artifacts.body: Agents shall be defined as markdown files that are fully editable in the GUI and synchronizable from disk.

artifacts.title: Proposal-gated writes
artifacts.body: All agent-initiated changes to project data shall be diverted into proposals that require explicit human approval before taking effect.

artifacts.title: User-composable crews
artifacts.body: Users shall compose multi-agent architectures using an org-chart editor (department groups, hierarchical layout) and a network-diagram editor; a default crew shall ship with each workspace; crews shall accept human members with employees/agents/all views.

artifacts.title: Unified kanban
artifacts.body: A kanban board shall track work items for both AI agents and human workers, including agent handoffs to humans.

artifacts.title: Manual, scheduled and triggered automation
artifacts.body: Agent utilization shall be launchable manually, on cron schedules, and on project events (triggers).

artifacts.title: Code repository operation
artifacts.body: Agents shall optionally operate on connected code repositories in addition to OpenV data.

artifacts.title: Tool-surface access for maintenance sessions
artifacts.body:
The MCP tool server shall authenticate with any credential the API already accepts for the operations it performs - an agent run token injected by a platform-launched run, or a workspace runner key - so that agent sessions outside a platform run reach project data through the same tool surface as platform runs, rather than through bespoke API scripts.

The presented credential, not the tool server, shall determine what the session may read and write: a run token stays scoped to its run's project and its agent's write mode, while a workspace runner key carries workspace-wide editor rights and no proposal gating.

artifacts.title: Maintenance loop covered by tools
artifacts.body:
The tool surface shall cover every step of the requirements-maintenance loop an agent performs in session: reading project data, editing artifacts and links, recording verification evidence, reporting verification coverage and traceability gaps, and capturing baselines. No maintenance step shall require an agent to bypass the tool surface with raw API calls.

Bulk project export is excluded by design: it is a file-level backup operation, and exposing it as a tool would invite agents to pull a whole project into context against the lean-context rule.

artifacts.title: Seed updates reach unedited agents only
artifacts.body: When a platform release changes a seeded agent definition, the system shall update an existing workspace agent field by field, and shall update a field only where that field still holds the exact value written by a previous release of the same seed. The system shall preserve every field a workspace member has changed.

artifacts.title: Locking an agent against automatic updates
artifacts.body: The system shall let a workspace administrator lock an individual agent, and shall exclude a locked agent from every automatic seed update, regardless of whether the agent's fields still match a previous release of the seed. The system shall keep the lock state in the agent's definition file as well as in the agent registry, shall show the lock state in the agent list and the agent editor, and shall return a locked agent to automatic updates when an administrator removes the lock.

artifacts.title: Recovering a hidden side panel
artifacts.body: The system shall let a reader set each side panel to pinned, auto-hiding or hidden, and shall leave an edge strip in place of a panel that is not pinned. The system shall open the panel when the reader clicks that strip, including when the panel is hidden, and shall keep the opened panel visible until the reader dismisses it. The system shall open an auto-hiding panel on hover, and shall not open a hidden panel on hover.

artifacts.title: In-app and email notifications
artifacts.body: The system shall notify a member in the application when a proposal awaits their review, when a run they launched fails, when an interview they created completes, when an artifact enters review in a project they edit, when someone mentions them in a comment, when a review is requested of them, and when a workspace budget threshold is reached. The system shall push a new notification live to the member's open sessions, shall never notify a member of their own action, and shall let each member read notifications, mark them read and opt out of email. When an operator configures a mail transport, the system shall also email the high-signal types; otherwise the system shall send no email and shall not fail.

artifacts.title: Proposal review controls
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor approve or reject proposals one at a time or in bulk. The system shall cap the proposals one run may raise at a fixed number and shall refuse further proposals from that run once the cap is reached. A run shall be able to name a not-yet-approved artifact proposal by a temporary reference so that a link proposal in the same run resolves to the real artifact when both are approved, and the system shall fail the link proposal when the artifact proposal is rejected or approved after it. A run that finishes with pending proposals shall await approval and shall succeed or fail only when its last proposal is resolved.

artifacts.title: Crew templates and portability
artifacts.body: The system shall ship built-in crew templates that instantiate against a workspace's seeded agents, shall let a member clone a crew, and shall export a crew as a portable document and import one into another workspace. An export shall carry agents by slug and shall omit human members; an import shall skip a node whose agent slug the target workspace lacks together with its edges, and shall refuse a document of the wrong kind or without a name.

artifacts.title: Board-driven agent runs
artifacts.body: Moving a board card into a column owned by an agent shall enqueue a run of that agent for the card, and the run's progress and outcome shall be written to the card's activity feed. A crew hand-off to a human member shall create a board card assigned to that member instead of launching a run.

artifacts.title: Agent model, effort and tool allowlist
artifacts.body: Each agent definition shall name its provider, its model chosen from a catalog or typed freely, an optional reasoning effort, an allowlist of the tools it may use, a turn cap and a timeout. The runner shall pass the model and effort to the vendor CLI in that vendor's own terms, mapping an effort the vendor lacks to its nearest tier and omitting one it cannot express. The runner shall grant an agent only the tools on its allowlist. A workspace admin shall set each provider's authentication mode and default model, and a runner shall report the CLIs, sign-in state and models it detects on its host.

artifacts.title: AI context surface
artifacts.body: The system shall render a project as a compact outline map, one line per artifact carrying its stable reference, title, non-draft status and inline link annotations, and shall serve the map both as an agent tool and as an API endpoint. The system shall render the map from a named baseline on request, stamped with the baseline's name and capture time. The system shall serve a one-call context bundle for an artifact addressed by reference or identifier, holding its body, ancestor path, children and every linked artifact with an excerpt. Every tool that takes an artifact identifier shall also accept its stable reference.

artifacts.title: Hierarchical versioned modules
artifacts.body:
The system shall organize artifacts as hierarchical, ordered modules within projects, with parent/child structure and stable ordering. Creating an artifact relative to another — before it or after it — shall place the new artifact in that position within its sibling group rather than at the end of the group.

Dragging an artifact onto another shall both reorder and re-parent, decided by where the pointer is released: the upper half shall place it before that artifact, the lower left after it, and the lower right shall make it a child of it. The artifact under the pointer shall show which of the three would happen before the drop is made. An artifact shall never be droppable into its own subtree, and a drop that would change nothing shall be refused rather than written. A drop into a collapsed artifact shall expand it, so the moved artifact remains visible.

artifacts.title: Typed artifacts with attributes
artifacts.body: The system shall support typed artifacts (persona, user need, requirement, design item, test case, hazard, heading, description and other), each carrying free-form attributes and, where the workspace or project defines them, typed attributes validated on write.

artifacts.title: Semantically constrained links
artifacts.body: The system shall enforce link-type rules: verifies (test case to requirement), validates (test case to user need), satisfies (design item to requirement), derives-from (requirement to user need), decomposes-to (requirement to requirement), mitigates (design item to hazard), impacts (any artifact to any artifact) and relates-to (any artifact to any artifact, bidirectional). The system shall reject a link whose end types the rule for its type does not allow, with an error naming the rule.

artifacts.title: Artifact version history
artifacts.body: Every artifact edit shall create a retrievable version, and any prior version shall be restorable.

artifacts.title: Project baselines
artifacts.body: The system shall capture immutable named baselines of a project's full artifact and link state.

artifacts.title: Project download in every format
artifacts.body:
The system shall offer one download action per project, from which a member chooses the output format. The system shall render a project as a PDF specification, a Word document, structured JSON, a CSV table and a ReqIF interchange file. The PDF and the Word document shall include V&V status. The JSON shall carry everything a project import restores.

The system shall prepare one project snapshot per download and render every format from that snapshot, so that the same request yields the same content in whichever format a member chose. The system shall download a baseline's snapshot in place of the live project when the member has selected a baseline.

artifacts.title: Visible artifact references
artifacts.body: The system shall show each artifact's stable reference wherever a reader might cite it: leading the artifact detail heading, on every non-section row of the project tree, as a Reference row in the details table, qualifying every traceability row, and titling each artifact in the PDF and DOCX reports. A section shows its document number in place of a reference.

artifacts.title: Document section numbering
artifacts.body: The system shall number heading artifacts hierarchically (1, 1.1, 1.2, 2) from their position in document order, shall number headings only, and shall number a heading nested under a non-heading within its nearest heading ancestor. Reordering the document shall renumber it while stable references stay fixed. Numbers shall be computed rather than stored, and served only when a list request asks for them, in which case the whole project is numbered rather than the returned page.

artifacts.title: Requirement wording convention
artifacts.body:
Each workspace shall carry a requirement quality rule set: the normative convention its requirements are written in — ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 "shall" or RFC 2119 must/should/may — and the severity, including off, of each wording rule.

Each project shall inherit its workspace's rule set until it stores an override, and each level shall store only the keys it overrides, so a project that re-grades one rule keeps its workspace's convention. A workspace that has stored nothing shall resolve to the "shall" convention.

The linter shall judge wording against the resolved convention, so that a keyword binding under one convention is not reported as weak wording under the other, and shall report a keyword belonging to the other convention so that one project does not drift between the two vocabularies.

artifacts.title: Copy, paste and duplicate artifacts
artifacts.body: The artifact context menu shall offer copy, paste before, paste after and duplicate alongside its create actions. Copying shall take an artifact's content — type, title, body and attributes — and not its identity, its links or its figures, so that a copy never asserts traceability nobody created. Pasting shall place the copy as a sibling of the artifact acted on, immediately before or after it, and duplicating shall place a copy of that artifact directly after it. A pasted artifact shall be titled so a reader can tell it from its original. Paste shall be offered but unusable until something has been copied.

artifacts.title: Quality rules visible to people and agents
artifacts.body:
The resolved rule set shall be visible to everyone who writes requirements, human or agent.

Workspace admins shall set the house style and project editors shall set a project's override from settings. Each setting shall list every value it permits exactly once, preselected to the value in force at that level. A project setting that differs from its workspace value shall carry an override warning naming the workspace value, so that a local value is never mistaken for an inherited one.

Agents shall reach the same rules through the tool surface, and the project orientation map an agent reads before drafting shall state the convention in force, so that an agent writes to the project's house style rather than inferring one from the artifacts it happens to read.

artifacts.title: Referencing figures and linked artifacts in descriptions
artifacts.body:
An artifact's description shall let its author cite a figure or another artifact by typing a hash, which shall offer that artifact's own figures and the artifacts it is already linked to, filtered by what is typed, and shall insert the chosen reference into the text.

The offer shall be confined to what the artifact is already connected to, so that a description cannot cite an artifact with no traceability link behind it. A hash inside a word shall not open the offer, so that ordinary text such as a URL fragment is left alone.

A reference in a rendered description shall be a link: following an artifact reference shall select that artifact, and following a figure reference shall open that figure without leaving the description. Text that merely resembles a reference — a markdown heading, a hash inside a word — shall be left as written, and trailing punctuation shall not be absorbed into the link.

A description shall preserve the line breaks its author typed.

artifacts.title: Advisory quality findings
artifacts.body:
Quality findings shall be advisory. The linter shall score an artifact and explain each finding in terms of the rule that produced it, and shall never reject, gate or divert a write, whoever the author is.

A quality report shall carry the rule set it was produced under, because the same wording scores differently between conventions and a score without its rules cannot be read.

artifacts.title: Panels that yield their space
artifacts.body:
The project navigation and the artifact notes panel shall each offer three states: pinned, auto-hidden and hidden. The reader shall choose each panel's state independently, and the system shall remember that choice per person across sessions. A pinned panel shall take its width from the page. An auto-hidden panel shall present an edge affordance that opens the panel over the document on hover, and shall leave the document's layout unchanged. A hidden panel shall leave that affordance and nothing else, so that the reader can always bring the panel back.

The requirements workspace shall fit the height of the browser window at every window size, so that the window itself never scrolls. The artifact tree, the artifact document, the notes panel and the project navigation shall each scroll within their own bounds. The toolbar shall wrap to further rows without displacing the regions below it.

artifacts.title: Named actors and entities in the activity log
artifacts.body: The activity log shall name the person, agent or runner behind each recorded event and the artifact, link, work item, baseline, comment, test result or agent run it affected, showing those names alongside the stored identifiers so the audit trail reads without resolving identifiers by hand. A name that can no longer be resolved falls back to the identifier alone.

artifacts.title: Figures change only while editing
artifacts.body: Adding, replacing and removing a figure shall be possible only while editing the artifact that carries it. A view that presents an artifact for reading shall present its figures for reading, so that what the document shows cannot change by a stray click.

artifacts.title: Numbered figures with versioned images
artifacts.body:
An image attached to an artifact shall be a figure carrying a reference of its own, formed from the artifact's stable reference and a per-artifact figure number (REQ-17-FIG-1). A figure number shall be unique and shall never be issued twice: the counter shall only move forward, so that deleting a figure does not return its number to circulation and concurrent uploads cannot be allocated the same one. An artifact carrying no stable reference shall yield no figure reference rather than one that would collide once it has one.

A figure's file shall be stored and served under its figure reference, so that a downloaded image is named for what the document calls it, and the name the uploaded file had shall be retained alongside it.

A member shall be able to replace a figure's image with a new version. The figure shall keep its reference, superseded versions shall remain retrievable, and each version shall record who uploaded it and when.

A change of figure version shall take the artifact to a new version and shall write a note to the artifact's feed naming the figure and the versions it moved between. That artifact version shall not demote an approved artifact nor mark its links suspect, because the artifact's own statement is unchanged.

artifacts.title: Collapsible project menu groups
artifacts.body: The project navigation shall group its destinations under headings. The navigation shall collapse every group by default, so that each group occupies one line until the reader opens it. The navigation shall expand or collapse a group when the reader selects its heading. The system shall remember each choice per person across sessions. The navigation shall expand the group holding the reader's current page until the reader collapses that group.

artifacts.title: Choosing what a download contains
artifacts.body:
The download action shall let a member narrow what the download contains, and shall apply that choice to the prepared snapshot before rendering any format.

A member shall be able to select which top-level sections to include, and the system shall include every artifact beneath a selected section. A member shall be able to select which artifact types to include, and shall be able to exclude headings so that the download holds artifacts alone. The system shall include a traceability link only when the download contains both artifacts it joins.

A member shall be able to select which categories of attachment to include, and the system shall offer only the categories the project holds. The system shall deliver the rendered document and the selected attachment files together as one archive whenever a member selects any attachment category. The system shall name each attachment in the archive by its figure reference where it has one.

The system shall state what the current selection contains before the member commits to it. The system shall refuse a selection that matches no artifact.

artifacts.title: Artifact status workflow
artifacts.body: The system shall carry each artifact through the statuses draft, in review, approved and superseded, and shall accept only these transitions: draft to in review, in review to draft, in review to approved, and approved to superseded. The system shall refuse any other transition. The system shall treat superseded as terminal. The system shall demote a new content version of an approved artifact to draft while the archived approved version keeps its status. Approving an artifact shall clear the suspect flag on every link that touches it.

artifacts.title: Suspect links and the review queue
artifacts.body: The system shall mark a traceability link suspect when the content of either artifact it joins changes after the link was made, and shall keep the link suspect until a project editor confirms it. The system shall present a review queue per project that lists every suspect link and every artifact in review, so that a reviewer finds all pending review work in one place. The system shall not mark a link suspect for an attribute-only change or a figure version change.

artifacts.title: Baseline comparison
artifacts.body: The system shall compare a baseline against another baseline or against the live project, and shall report the artifacts and links added, modified and removed between the two. For a modified artifact the system shall name which fields changed and shall show the old and the new value. The system shall treat a link that was recreated with a new identifier but the same ends and type as unchanged.

artifacts.title: Artifact search
artifacts.body: The system shall let a member search artifact titles and bodies by text across every project the member can access in the active workspace, and shall return only artifacts from projects the member holds at least viewer access to. The system shall use an index-assisted search where the database supports it and shall fall back to a sequential search where it does not, with identical results.

artifacts.title: Semantic search and duplicate detection
artifacts.body: When an operator configures an embedding provider, the system shall compute a vector embedding for each artifact's title and body, shall re-embed an artifact only when its content or the embedding model changes, and shall offer nearest-neighbour search and duplicate-candidate detection over those embeddings per project. When no embedding provider is configured the system shall behave as if the capability did not exist, and shall make no outbound call. An embedding failure shall never fail the artifact write that triggered it.

artifacts.title: Typed attribute definitions
artifacts.body: The system shall let a workspace admin define custom artifact attributes for the workspace and a project editor define them for one project, each with a name, a type of text, number, date or enumeration, an optional list of permitted values, and the artifact types it applies to. The system shall validate an artifact's attribute values against the definitions in force for its project on every write, and shall reject a value of the wrong type or outside the permitted list. A project definition shall take precedence over a workspace definition of the same name.

artifacts.title: Project import
artifacts.body: The system shall create a project from an OpenV JSON export or from a ReqIF interchange document. The system shall assign fresh identifiers at version one to every imported artifact, shall reconstruct the parent hierarchy, links, status and attributes, and shall preserve each artifact's stable reference. The system shall reject a malformed document, or an enumerated attribute value outside its declared values, with a validation error rather than a partial import. The system shall carry attachment metadata but not attachment files across an import.

artifacts.title: Project templates
artifacts.body: The system shall let a project editor save a project as a workspace template, and shall let any member create a new project from a built-in or workspace template. A workspace template shall be visible only inside its workspace.

artifacts.title: Same-site session on every deployment
artifacts.body: The system shall serve the application and its API so that the session cookie is a first-party cookie in every supported browser, including browsers that block third-party cookies outright. A deployment shall be able to place the API behind the application's own origin, and a deployment that keeps the API on a separate site shall mark the session and sign-on cookies as partitioned. A member on a phone or tablet browser shall be able to sign in and stay signed in for the session lifetime.

artifacts.title: Layout by screen width
artifacts.body: The application shall select its layout from the width of the screen. The application shall use a phone layout at 640 pixels and below and a narrow tablet layout at 900 pixels and below. On a phone the application shall present the project navigation as a drawer opened from a button in the header. On a touch device the application shall treat the auto-hiding panel state as hidden. Every edge strip that recovers a panel shall be at least 44 pixels wide. No view shall scroll the page horizontally at 360 pixels wide. Content that does not fit a region shall scroll within that region, and the application shall not clip it. The application shall size itself to the visible viewport, so that a browser toolbar never covers a bottom control. The application shall respect the device's safe-area insets.

artifacts.title: Stacked requirements workspace on narrow screens
artifacts.body: Below the tablet breakpoint the requirements workspace shall present its tree, document and notes as one region at a time, switched by a control that stays visible, each scrolling within its own bounds, so that the workspace still fits the window without clipping any of the three. Selecting an artifact in the tree shall switch to the document. The guided definition wizard shall present its step rail as a progress bar and its assistant as a sheet that opens over the step on the same widths.

artifacts.title: Touch alternatives for every drag, hover and right-click action
artifacts.body: Every action the application offers through a drag, a hover or a right-click shall also be reachable through a tap. Each artifact row shall carry a menu button that opens the same actions as its context menu. A member shall be able to move an artifact to a chosen parent and position through a dialog, and the dialog shall apply the same placement rules as a drag. Figure actions shall be visible without hover on a touch device. Drag on the tree and the board shall use pointer events so that a finger can drag where the screen allows it.

artifacts.title: Tap targets and input sizing
artifacts.body: Every primary control shall present a tap target of at least 44 by 44 pixels on a touch device. Every text input, text area and select shall render at a font size of at least 16 pixels, so that a phone browser does not zoom on focus. Sign-in fields shall carry the autocomplete hints a password manager needs, chat composers shall carry a send key hint, and every table shall scroll horizontally within its own container. No dialog shall be wider than the viewport.

artifacts.title: Review and approval from a phone
artifacts.body: On a phone the review queue and the proposal list shall present each item as a card carrying its title, reference, the change it proposes and approve, reject and open actions, with the proposed change readable at 360 pixels wide. The notifications bell shall open a full-screen list whose entries lead to the mobile view of what they concern. Artifact comments and the V&V Assistant shall use the same single-column chat layout as the public interview page.

artifacts.title: Board actions without drag
artifacts.body: On a phone the board shall show one column at a time with a control to move between columns. Each card shall offer an action sheet with move to a chosen column, assign to a person or agent, and open, so that every board transition, including handing a card to an agent, is available without a drag.

artifacts.title: Runner control from a phone
artifacts.body: A member shall be able to lease, extend and end a cloud runner from a phone, and shall be able to complete a relayed vendor sign-in on it: the sign-in link shall open in the phone's browser, and the field that takes the returned code or address shall accept a paste from a password manager and submit with the keyboard's send key. A member shall be able to launch, watch, retry and cancel a run from a phone.

artifacts.title: Installable application and push notifications
artifacts.body: The application shall remain installable as a standalone web application on phones and tablets, shall declare screenshots and shortcuts to the review queue, the board and notifications, and shall keep serving live content without caching a shell. When a member opts in on a device, the system shall deliver the high-signal notification types to that device by web push, shall store one subscription per device, and shall let the member withdraw the subscription.

artifacts.title: Mobile test coverage
artifacts.body: The end-to-end suite shall run the smoke journey on a WebKit engine and on a phone and a tablet device profile in addition to desktop Chrome, and shall run a mobile journey covering sign-in, approving a review item, moving a board card through its action sheet, and reaching the cloud runner sign-in screen. A viewport check shall fail the suite when any view scrolls horizontally at 360 pixels wide.

artifacts.title: Mobile support plan 2026-09-07
artifacts.body:
# Mobile support plan

Status: approved and implemented through Phase 3, 2026-09-07 — see
section 8 for what shipped and what is deferred. Evidence base: the frontend
readiness review in `docs/assessments/2026-09-07-mobile-readiness.md`.
Requirements recorded in the OpenV Platform project under **Mobile**
(NEED-13, REQ-101 … REQ-110, DES-23, TC-50).

## 1. Where we are

OpenV's frontend is a desktop application. The facts that matter:

- **iOS cannot sign in to production.** The frontend and API live on two
  different `up.railway.app` hosts, which browsers treat as different *sites*
  (the suffix is on the Public Suffix List), so the session cookie is a
  third-party cookie (`SameSite=None`). Safari drops third-party cookies
  outright, and every browser on iOS is Safari underneath. Sign-in appears to
  succeed, the next request answers 401, and the app bounces back to the
  login page. Android Chrome still works but is on the same road. Self-hosted
  deployments on one domain are unaffected.
- **No responsive layer.** Six media queries in the whole codebase, all in
  leaf components (lightbox, gallery, project cards, help panel); no
  component knows the screen width; styling is inline pixel widths. The
  requirements workspace needs about 460 px before the document pane has any
  width at all, and the guided wizard needs 852 px with no wrapping. Both
  clip overflow rather than scroll, by design (REQ-53 fits the window).
- **No touch layer.** Every drag is HTML5 drag-and-drop, which touch
  browsers do not synthesise: reparenting an artifact and launching an agent
  from the board are drag-only. Seven artifact actions live behind a
  right-click menu. Figure actions appear on hover. Panels in auto-hide mode
  open on hover and are recovered through a 10 px edge strip.
- **Input details bite:** every field is 14 px, so iOS zooms on focus and
  stays zoomed; the login card is a fixed 380 px and overflows an iPhone SE;
  `100vh` is used where `100dvh` is needed, so bottom bars sit under the
  Safari toolbar.
- **What already works:** the app is installable (manifest with maskable
  icons, `display: standalone`, a deliberately non-caching service worker);
  routes are code-split so the heavy grid and graph libraries stay off the
  first load; the public interview chat is a genuine phone-first screen and
  works on iOS because it uses no cookie; the crew graph (Cytoscape) already
  handles touch; the design tokens support dark mode and system preference.

## 2. Who needs mobile, for what

| Persona | Jobs on a phone or tablet | Today |
|---|---|---|
| PER-4 External stakeholder | Answer an interview from a link | Works |
| PER-1 Solo founder, PER-2 Company admin | Approve or reject proposals and reviews; read a requirement someone linked; reply to a comment or ask the V&V Assistant; see a run fail and retry it; act on a budget alert; start a cloud runner and sign an agent in from the browser relay | Blocked on iOS; unusable layout elsewhere |
| PER-3 Team contributor | Move a board card, comment on it, hand work to an agent; read requirements on a tablet in a meeting or on the shop floor | Same |

Not mobile jobs, and explicitly out of scope: authoring long documents,
building crews, editing the traceability matrix, resizing columns, installing
the Agent Connector.

The transient runner with browser-relayed sign-in (REQ-57, REQ-58) is the
feature that makes a phone genuinely useful: a founder can lease a runner,
sign Claude in by pasting a code, and launch agents from anywhere with
nothing installed. The plan protects that path first.

## 3. Strategy: one responsive web app, installed as a PWA

Recommendation: make the existing React app responsive and touch-capable and
ship it through the PWA shell that already exists. Not a native app, not a
wrapper.

- The product is a live collaborative tool with no offline requirement; the
  service worker's no-cache stance stays.
- One codebase, one deployment, no store review, and every fix ships through
  the existing promote-to-release path.
- Web Push reaches installed PWAs on iOS 16.4 and later and on Android, so
  notifications do not require a native app.
- A Capacitor wrapper can be added later without redoing any of this work if
  store presence or native share sheets ever matter.

## 4. Phases

### Phase 0 — Unblock iOS (one PR, the prerequisite for everything else)

Serve the API and the app from **one origin**. Two ways; the first is
recommended because it needs no DNS and removes cross-site cookies entirely:

- **A. Proxy the API through the frontend's nginx.** Add
  `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://openv.railway.internal:8080; }` (the
  API's Railway private domain) with `proxy_buffering off` and
  `proxy_read_timeout` raised for SSE, `client_max_body_size 32m` to match
  the API's body cap, and forwarded headers. Build the frontend with
  `REACT_APP_API_URL` empty and make the client default to a relative
  `/api` on the same origin. Then the cookie is first-party,
  `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` comes off, `SameSite=Lax` applies, CORS is unused, and
  the CSP `connect-src` collapses to `'self'`. Self-hosted compose can do the
  same or keep two ports.
- **B. A custom domain pair** (`app.example` and `api.example`) under one
  registrable domain, keeping CORS. Needs a domain and DNS; still cross-origin
  for CORS purposes but same-site for cookies.

Belt and braces in the same PR: set the `Partitioned` attribute (CHIPS) on
the session and OIDC cookies when `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` is on, so any
remaining cross-site deployment works on Safari 18.4 and later. Add a WebKit
project and an iPhone project to Playwright so the sign-in journey is run on
the engine that failed.

Effort: one to two days. Risk: SSE through nginx (buffering), upload size
cap, and `/api/v1/public/connector/download` (27 MB) through the proxy;
keep that one on the API origin or raise the cap for it.

### Phase 1 — Layout foundation

Make the shell responsive without redesigning any view.

- A `useViewport` hook and two breakpoints: phone (≤ 640 px) and narrow
  tablet (≤ 900 px), exposed as a context so views can branch.
- `ProjectLayout`: below the phone breakpoint the side navigation becomes an
  off-canvas drawer behind a 44 px menu button; the auto-hide mode is treated
  as hidden on touch; edge strips grow to 44 px.
- The requirements workspace: below the tablet breakpoint the three columns
  become one stacked view with a segmented control (Tree, Document, Notes),
  each scrolling within its own bounds, so REQ-53's fit-the-window contract
  holds on every width instead of clipping.
- The guided wizard: rail collapses to a top progress bar; the assistant
  panel becomes a bottom sheet.
- Global fixes: `100dvh` and safe-area insets; 16 px inputs; every table in
  an `overflow-x: auto` wrapper; login and the unclamped modals capped at
  the viewport; `viewport-fit=cover` and the Apple web-app meta tags;
  `autoComplete` on the login form; `enterKeyHint` on chat composers.

Effort: three to five days.

### Phase 2 — The mobile jobs

Make the review-and-act flows first class on a phone, in this order:

1. **Review queue and proposals**: card list with approve, reject and open
   actions; the proposal diff readable at 360 px.
2. **Notifications**: the bell becomes a full-screen list; deep links land
   on mobile views.
3. **Reading requirements**: the stacked workspace from Phase 1 plus a
   reference search that jumps to a ref; comments and the V&V Assistant on
   the same chat skeleton the interview page uses.
4. **Board**: one column at a time with a pager; a card's action sheet
   offers *Move to…* and *Assign to agent*, so launching an agent no longer
   depends on drag.
5. **Runner card**: start, extend and end a cloud runner; the relayed
   sign-in screen sized for a phone (this is where a paste from a password
   manager has to work).
6. **Runs**: list, detail, retry and cancel.

Effort: one to two weeks.

### Phase 3 — Touch parity for editing

- A kebab button on every artifact row opens the same menu as right-click.
- *Move to…* dialog (choose parent and position) as the touch alternative to
  drag, using the existing `planMove` logic.
- Convert drags to pointer events with `touch-action: none` on the handle,
  so tree and board drag also work with a finger where the screen allows it.
- Figure actions always visible on touch devices; the figure reference
  autocomplete gets a tap-to-insert menu.

Effort: about a week.

### Phase 4 — Installability and polish

- Manifest screenshots and shortcuts (Review queue, Board, Notifications).
- Web Push for the high-signal notification types: a VAPID key pair, a
  push-subscription table, a subscribe endpoint, and the service worker's
  `push` handler; opt-in per device.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`; raise the muted-text contrast token to 4.5:1;
  a server-side thumbnail size for figures and a right-sized logo.

Effort: about a week, of which push is most of it.

## 5. Testing

- Playwright projects: Desktop Chrome (existing), WebKit, iPhone 13,
  Pixel 5, iPad portrait. The smoke journey runs on all of them; a mobile
  journey covers sign-in, review queue approve, board move via action sheet,
  and starting a cloud runner up to the relay screen.
- A viewport contract test: at 360 px wide no view scrolls horizontally and
  every primary action is at least 44 px.
- Lighthouse mobile in CI as an informational score, not a gate.

## 6. Requirements recorded

NEED-13 *Act on my product from my phone* and, deriving from it, REQ-101
same-site session, REQ-102 responsive shell, REQ-103 stacked requirements
workspace, REQ-104 touch alternatives for every drag, hover and right-click
action, REQ-105 tap targets and input sizing, REQ-106 mobile review and
approval, REQ-107 board actions without drag, REQ-108 runner control from a
phone, REQ-109 installable app metadata and push, REQ-110 mobile test
coverage; DES-23 same-origin API proxy; TC-50 mobile journey suite.

## 7. Decisions for the maintainer

1. Phase 0 option A (nginx proxy, recommended) or B (custom domain pair).
2. Whether Web Push is worth its backend surface now or waits.
3. Whether a store presence will ever matter (it changes nothing in Phases
   0 to 3; it decides whether Phase 4 grows a Capacitor wrapper).

## 8. Implementation status (2026-09-07)

Decisions taken: Phase 0 option A (nginx proxy); Web Push deferred; no
store presence planned.

Shipped, in one PR on top of this plan:

- **Phase 0** — `frontend/nginx.conf` proxies `/api/` to `API_UPSTREAM`
  (re-resolved through the container's DNS by
  `frontend/docker-entrypoint.d/40-openv-api-proxy.sh`); the client defaults
  to a relative `/api` in production builds; the CSP collapses to `'self'`;
  `Partitioned` on cross-site cookies; a WebKit Playwright project. The
  connector download goes through the proxy unbuffered, so no special case
  was needed. Production needs the variable changes in `docs/railway.md`
  (`API_UPSTREAM` on the frontend; `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES` off and `PUBLIC_URL`
  on the frontend origin for the API) at the next promotion.
- **Phase 1** — `hooks/useViewport`; drawer navigation with a top bar below
  900 px; the stacked Tree / Document / Notes requirements module; the
  wizard's progress strip and assistant bottom sheet; 16 px fields on touch,
  `100dvh`, table wrappers, safe-area helpers, reduced motion, clamped login
  and modals, viewport and installed-app meta tags.
- **Phase 2** — notifications panel full-width on phones; suspect links as
  cards with 44 px controls; the board shows one column at a time with a
  pager and a card actions sheet offering *Open card* and *Move to <column>*
  (the same move as a drop, so it launches an agent from To Do). Runs,
  proposals and the requirements page reuse the stacked layout and table
  wrappers rather than new mobile views.
- **Phase 3** — every artifact row has a visible ⋯ actions button opening
  the right-click menu; the menu gains *Move to…* (target artifact and
  before / after / inside, validated by `planMove`); on coarse pointers a
  grip handle drags rows through pointer events with `touch-action: none`
  on the handle only, so the list still scrolls.
- **Phase 4 (part)** — manifest shortcuts and categories; muted text raised
  to 4.6:1; reduced-motion media query.
- **Testing** — `e2e/tests/mobile.spec.ts` runs in iPhone 13 (WebKit) and
  Pixel 5 (Chromium) projects: drawer navigation, the stacked module, and
  the no-horizontal-scroll contract on every page it visits.

Deferred, each a follow-up of its own:

- Web Push (VAPID keys, a subscription table, a subscribe endpoint, the
  worker's `push` handler) — REQ-109 remains partially met (installable,
  no push).
- The runner card and the relayed sign-in screen sized for a phone
  (REQ-108); they work through the responsive shell but were not reworked.
- Figure actions on touch and the tap-to-insert reference menu; server-side
  figure thumbnails; manifest screenshots; an iPad project and Lighthouse in
  CI.

artifacts.title: Mobile readiness assessment 2026-09-07
artifacts.body:
Scope: `frontend/` at `81030f9` (master after PR #298). 35,511 lines of
TS/TSX across 7 CSS files; styling is overwhelmingly inline `style={{}}`
objects, so almost nothing is reachable by a media query. Companion to
`docs/plans/mobile-support.md`.

**Headline: the app is a desktop-only application.** There is no responsive
layer, no touch layer, and on the production Railway topology no working
sign-in on iOS Safari. It is installable as a PWA, but the installed app is
the same desktop layout.

## 1. Responsive design

Exactly ten `@media` occurrences, six of them responsive, all in leaf
components: `ImageLightbox.css:88`, `ImageGallery.css:145`,
`ProjectList.css:331`, `ImageUploadInput.css:57` (all `max-width: 768px`)
and `HelpSidebar.css:179,189` (1024 and 768 px). No layout container has
one. No component reads the screen width: a grep for `innerWidth`,
`matchMedia`, `ResizeObserver`, `visualViewport` finds only the theme's
`prefers-color-scheme` check.

Fixed-pixel layouts that decide the minimum usable width:

| View | Fixed widths | Minimum before content is legible |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectLayout.tsx:171-212` | shell `100vh`/`overflow:hidden`; nav `width/minWidth 200`; edge strip 10 px | 200 px before any view |
| `ModuleView.tsx:1084-1750` | tree column 400 px default (`min 200`, `max 800`), notes 320 px (`min 250`), two 10 px resize handles, 40 px padding, `overflow: hidden` | about 460 px with the document pane at zero |
| `GuidedWizard.tsx:1654-1677` + `StepShell.tsx:43` + `GuidedChatPanel.tsx:510` | rail 220 px, chat panel 340 px, no `flexWrap` | 852 px with the nav |
| `KanbanBoard.tsx:325-345` | columns `flex: 0 0 260px`, row scrolls horizontally | one column visible on a phone |
| `TraceabilityMatrix.tsx:226-303` | pinned 240 px column, further `minWidth` 200 to 280 | about 1160 px |
| `CrewBuilder.tsx:669`, `AgentsPage.tsx:138`, `AgentRunsPage.tsx:330`, `ImpactView.tsx:112`, `ManualView.tsx:164-169` | side panels of 320, 320, 460, 320 and 260 px | two-column with no fallback |
| `Login.tsx:72`, `CreateOrgModal.tsx:65`, `WorkItemDrawer.tsx:150` | 380, 400 and 420 px with no `maxWidth` | overflow on an iPhone SE |

The shared `Modal`, `ConfirmDialog` and `PromptDialog` are correctly clamped
to the viewport. Twelve of fifteen tables have fixed-width headers and no
horizontal scroll wrapper. `100vh` is used in about ten places where
`100dvh` is needed.

The `overflow: hidden` shell is REQ-53's fit-the-window contract working as
designed; on a narrow screen it converts every overflow into clipped,
unreachable content rather than a scroll.

## 2. Touch and pointer

- Every drag is HTML5 `draggable` plus `dataTransfer`
  (`ArtifactList.tsx:213-272`, `KanbanBoard.tsx:331-377`); a grep for
  touch or pointer handlers in `src/` finds none. Touch browsers do not
  synthesise these events. Reparenting an artifact is drag-only
  (`utils/artifactDrag.ts:10-13`) and launching an agent from the board is
  drag-only (`KanbanBoard.tsx:320`).
- The Cytoscape crew canvas (`CrewCanvas.tsx:165-340`) is the one exception
  and already handles tap and drag by touch, with 30 px nodes.
- The artifact context menu is right-click only (`ArtifactList.tsx:207-212`)
  and carries seven actions with no other entry point; iOS shows its native
  callout on long-press instead of firing `contextmenu`.
- Panel auto-hide opens on hover (`panelMode.ts:47`), is persisted per
  person, and is recovered through a 10 px strip; on touch it behaves as
  hidden. Figure actions sit in a hover overlay (`ImageGallery.css:43-45`).
  Column resizing binds mouse events only (`ModuleView.tsx:151-197`).
- 151 `title` tooltips never render on touch; several carry the only
  explanation of a control.
- Tap targets: edge strips and resize handles 10 px; tree chevron 14 px;
  download-wizard checkboxes 16 px; nav section headers about 26 px tall;
  most chips `padding: 1px 6px`. Only the help button (60 px) and the
  interview composer (44 px) meet the 44 px guideline. 117 `fontSize`
  values of 11 px or less.

## 3. Viewport and PWA

`index.html` has a correct viewport meta without `user-scalable=no`, a
theme colour, one apple-touch-icon and the manifest link; it lacks
`viewport-fit=cover` and the Apple web-app meta tags. `manifest.json` is
complete: `display: standalone`, `id`, `start_url`, `scope`, maskable and
plain icons at 192 and 512 px; no screenshots or shortcuts, and
`orientation: any` lets an installed phone app launch into a portrait layout
it cannot render. `sw.js` deliberately caches nothing (documented
rationale: live collaborative app), so there is no offline mode, no push,
and no stale-shell risk; registration is inline in `index.tsx:30-37`.

## 4. Navigation

`ProjectLayout` is a permanent 200 px left rail with no drawer, hamburger
or tab bar. `panelMode` is a preference, not a response to width; the
default is pinned. Nothing adapts to the screen.

## 5. Mobile-specific views

`InterviewChat.tsx` is the only phone-first screen: a fluid column capped at
640 px, the standard header, scrolling list and fixed composer, 80 percent
bubbles with word wrapping, a 44 px composer, no cookie (`withCredentials:
false`), so it works on iOS. Its faults are `100vh`, a 14 px textarea
(focus zoom) and a Ctrl-Enter-only shortcut beside the send button.

## 6. Inputs

`index.css:116-125` sets 14 px on every input, textarea and select, so iOS
zooms on focus and stays zoomed; several components go to 12 or 13 px. The
body editor's `#` reference autocomplete is driven by arrow, Enter and Tab
keys (`ArtifactEditor.tsx:196-211`), none of which a soft keyboard offers,
though entries can be tapped. No `capture` attribute on file inputs, which
is correct (the OS offers camera and library). No date inputs exist. No
`inputMode`, `autoCapitalize` or `enterKeyHint`; `autoComplete` only appears
as `off`, so the login form gets no password-manager autofill.

## 7. Authentication on mobile

`api/client.ts:34-41` is cookie-only (`withCredentials: true`) with no
bearer fallback. Production sets `CROSS_SITE_COOKIES=true`, so
`handlers.go:187-192` issues the session as `SameSite=None; Secure`. The two
`up.railway.app` hosts are different registrable sites (the suffix is on the
Public Suffix List), so the cookie is third-party. Safari blocks third-party
cookies unconditionally and every iOS browser is WebKit: sign-in appears to
succeed, the next request answers 401, and the response interceptor
(`client.ts:70-79`) sends the user back to the login page. The cookie is not
`Partitioned` (Go's `http.Cookie` field is unused), Safari also caps
`SameSite=None` lifetimes, and the three `EventSource` streams inherit the
same problem. The public interview route is the one flow that works.
Self-hosted deployments on one domain get `SameSite=Lax` and are unaffected.

## 8. Performance

No client-side PDF or DOCX libraries (exports are server-side). Routes are
code-split well (`App.tsx:28-59`): the 1.1 MB ag-grid chunk and the 434 KB
Cytoscape chunk stay off the first load. The main bundle is 616 KB
uncompressed and first render waits on three sequential API calls. The
navbar logo is a 180 KB PNG drawn at 56 px; gallery thumbnails load
full-resolution attachments; no `loading="lazy"` or `srcSet` anywhere; gzip
on, brotli off; source maps are shipped.

## 9. Accessibility that affects mobile

Pinch-zoom is preserved; the token system supports dark mode and
`prefers-color-scheme`; body text contrast is strong. The muted text token
(`#7f8c8d` on white) is about 3.6:1, below AA, and it is used for much of
the small secondary text; `--neutral` on white is about 2.6:1. No
`prefers-reduced-motion` handling; the board's live-run indicator pulses
indefinitely.

## 10. Tests

`e2e/playwright.config.ts` has one project, Desktop Chrome. No WebKit, no
device profile, no viewport override. Nothing in CI exercises the engine
where the cookie blocker lives.

## Ranked obstacles

Phone: (1) sign-in impossible on iOS; (2) no responsive layer; (3) the
requirements workspace clips at any width under about 460 px; (4) all drag
dead on touch with no alternative for reparenting or handing a card to an
agent; (5) right-click-only artifact menu; (6) focus zoom on every field;
(7) the login card overflows small phones; (8) 10 to 24 px tap targets on
the controls that recover panels and expand branches; (9) auto-hide panel
mode is a trap on touch; (10) the guided wizard needs 852 px.

Tablet: (1) the iOS cookie blocker; (2) drag still dead, on a layout that
otherwise fits; (3) right-click and hover-only actions; (4) portrait breaks
the three-column views and the manifest allows portrait; (5) column
resizing and panel recovery are mouse-only.

product_profile.vision: OpenV is the multi-agent development suite that lets a solo founder (or a company) define products, manage requirements with full V&V traceability, and put AI agents to work as a real team - using each member's own AI subscription.
product_profile.problem_statement: Solo founders and small teams cannot afford dedicated requirements tooling plus a development team. Existing AI tools work from ad-hoc prompts with no traceability, no approval gates, and unpredictable execution that depends on whose laptop happens to be online.
product_profile.target_users: Solo founders defining and building products end-to-end; companies organizing requirements work across teams; external stakeholders contributing needs through interviews.

constraints.description: Consumer AI subscriptions (Claude/GPT/Gemini CLI logins) are personal-use: they run only on the member's own machine, never server-side. Company-wide AI is API-token only.
constraints.title: BYO-AI compliance

constraints.description: Provider API keys are never persisted in the database; worker keys, run tokens and pairing codes are stored as sha256 hashes with plaintext shown once.
constraints.title: No stored provider credentials

constraints.description: Nothing auto-starts on a member's machine; runners execute only while the user has the connector window open.
constraints.title: No background services on user machines
